Police charge another Tesla driver caught asleep in rush hour as cases pile up

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1254 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Tesla driver caught asleep behind the wheel on Ottawa’s Highway 417 during Tuesday’s rush hour now faces a careless driving charge from the Ontario Provincial Police.
  • In a recent development, the charge carries a $490 fine and six demerit points on conviction.
  • Sources indicate that OPP East Region posted about the stop Wednesday morning.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Tesla driver caught asleep behind the wheel on Ottawa’s Highway 417 during Tuesday’s rush hour now faces a careless driving charge from the Ontario Provincial Police. The photo OPP shared shows a new-generation Model Y in traffic.

In a recent development, the charge carries a $490 fine and six demerit points on conviction. It’s at least the fifth time this year Canadian police have gone public with a sleeping Tesla driver, and it’s not a coincidence that it’s happening as “Full Self-Driving” gets better.

Sources indicate that OPP East Region posted about the stop Wednesday morning. Police didn’t name the brand or the driver-assist system, but the message was clear: “even though your vehicle has an autonomous driving feature, drivers are still required to pay due care and attention when behind the wheel.”.

It has been revealed that according to OPP, the officer could see the driver’s eyes were closed and hands were off the steering wheel. Instead of lighting up the cruiser, police pulled in close to capture body camera footage first.

Careless driving isn’t a parking ticket in Ontario. The $490 is the set fine, but if the case goes to court, the Highway Traffic Act allows fines up to $2,000, up to six months in jail, and a licence suspension of up to two years.

Ottawa is the latest, but British Columbia has been dealing with this all year:.

This isn’t new in Canada either. Back in 2020, Alberta RCMP went further and criminally charged a Tesla driver caught sleeping on Autopilot at 150 km/h with dangerous driving.

The U.S. has the same problem with less enforcement. In September, Colorado State Patrol got a report of a sleeping Tesla driver on I-70 near Georgetown and never found the car. The same month, Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi pressed the DOT after NBC News found 43 videos of drivers apparently asleep in moving Teslas, 17 of them posted in 2026 alone.

Recent findings suggest that and in October, a driver told CHP he was asleep on FSD when his Tesla drove into a closed crash scene and hit a patrol car in Fairfield, California. Two officers were seriously injured.

In a recent development, A few years ago, FSD needed an intervention every few miles, so nobody was napping. You couldn’t.

Now FSD can handle long highway stretches without a takeover, and that’s exactly when supervision breaks down. A human asked to watch a system that’s right 99% of the time stops watching. That’s automation complacency, and it’s one of the most studied problems in aviation and driving research.

In a recent development, waymo learned this the hard way. In 2013, Google let employees use its highway driver-assist prototype and caught people falling asleep at highway speed. It decided a system that works most of the time but still needs a human to catch its mistakes was the worst of both worlds, and it went straight to driverless.

Tesla went the other way. It sells a Level 2 system called “Full Self-Driving” that’s good enough to lull people to sleep, and it puts the full responsibility on the human who’s now asleep.

It has been revealed that since FSD v12.4, Tesla has relied mainly on the cabin camera above the rearview mirror to make sure the driver is watching the road. But look at what Tesla’s own owner’s manual says about it: the camera “does not require full visibility of the driver’s eyes in order to monitor attentiveness,” and the system “is still active, for example, if the driver is wearing sunglasses.”.

In other words, it’s often judging head position, not whether your eyes are open. When it can’t see your hands, it falls back to asking for a bit of torque on the wheel, which a sleeping driver resting a hand on the rim can provide.

It has been revealed that the penalties are soft too. Five “strikeouts” suspend FSD for a week, and each strike is forgiven after three and a half days.

According to recent reports, and Tesla has been moving in the wrong direction. Musk stated in December 2025 that FSD v14.2.1 lets drivers text “depending on context of surrounding traffic.” In May 2026, he said v14.3.3 “nags less too.” When the car does detect drowsiness, Tesla’s alert reads “Drowsiness detected. Stay focused with FSD.” That pushes a tired driver to lean harder on the system instead of pulling over.

Compare that with GM’s Super Cruise, which uses a steering column camera with infrared LEDs to track head and eye position, and only works hands-free on pre-mapped highways.

The Ottawa driver had their eyes closed and their hands off the wheel in rush hour traffic, and the car was still driving when an officer pulled up beside it. Whatever Tesla’s camera was checking from a foot away, it hadn’t stopped the car before a cop in the next lane did.

It has been revealed that we’re glad Canadian police are treating this seriously. A $490 fine and six points is a real deterrent, and OPP’s message is the right one: no matter what Tesla calls it, you’re the driver.

People have been falling asleep at the wheel since driving started; many, if not most, have ended up in tragedy. At least with the self-driving cars, there is a margin of safety, especially for other drivers. These cars should monitor the driver better and pull off the road when it happens.

Recent findings suggest that but police can’t ticket their way out of this. These drivers aren’t edge cases anymore. They’re the predictable result of a system that drives well enough to make people relax, sold under a name that tells them relaxing is fine.

The fix is on Tesla’s side, and it isn’t complicated. Detect closed eyes, even behind sunglasses, which is what infrared eye-tracking is built for. When a driver doesn’t respond, slow down and pull over immediately instead of escalating warnings for minutes. Stop telling drowsy drivers to “stay focused with FSD.” And make the strike system actually sting.

Recent findings suggest that NHTSA already forced a recall of over 2 million Teslas in December 2023 over weak Autopilot monitoring. Three years later, people are still sleeping through rush hour on FSD.

Analysts eye 3.8% inflation as Fed weighs next move – Can crypto avoid a bearish December?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (534 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The next 24 hours could shape crypto’s December outlook.
  • Macro-wise, there is an key PCE inflation data release on Wednesday.
  • Should it show greater inflation than expected, this could reignite concerns around the Fed raising interest rates and in-turn weigh on riskier assets such as Bitcoin and the crypto sector.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The next 24 hours could shape crypto’s December outlook.

Macro-wise, there is an key PCE inflation data release on Wednesday. Markets are beginning to factor in what the data may show and the flexibility the Fed will then have.

Should it show greater inflation than expected, this could reignite concerns around the Fed raising interest rates and in-turn weigh on riskier assets such as Bitcoin and the crypto sector.

So, what is the market looking for?

Analysts who are monitoring CPI and PPI figures predict that PCE inflation will be running at 3.8%. Core PCE is seen rising by 3.2% year-on-year and by 0.29% month-on-month. If these estimates hold, core prices will have risen by at least 0.26% in nine of the past 12 months.

Together, this suggests that inflation remains sticky, leaving the Fed with less room to cut rates.

Oil prices are adding to these concerns. In October, oil increased by in excess of 15% to $120 per barrel; a high not seen since 2022. Interestingly, at the same time, the crypto market suffered a near 10% fall.

Clearly, there is an underlying macro relationship, whereby increasing oil prices can lead to inflation worries, accentuate interest rate issues and go on to add to strain on crypto.

Despite this, given that the next FOMC meeting is more than 2 weeks away, these views continue to largely stem from market sentiment. The bigger question therefore is: Will the data back this pessimistic narrative? Assuming inflation matches forecasts and the Fed adopts a less aggressive approach to rate hikes, could the crypto market avoid a bearish December?

Crypto is heading for one of its worst Q4 performances on record.

According to Coinglass, BTC has fallen by 32% in Q4, the worst-performing quarter since 2018, when it fell 43%. It now needs to fall just 11% points to equal that performance. While the market is now turning its attention to December as a potential turning point, there are growing macro risks that may affect this.

As highlighted in the post below, the U.S. President Donald Trump is at the moment working on a raft of newly introduced import duties against China, plus the European Union and 14 other countries. The Dollar Index (DXY) has also risen to a 20-month high.

Meanwhile, headlines that four oil tankers had been destroyed by naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz saw Brent oil rise 2% by the day’s end.

Taken together, tariffs, a stronger dollar and rising oil prices could keep inflation concerns elevated.

It has been revealed that against this backdrop, a crypto recovery in December still looks challenging. In this context, even if inflation figures are in line with expectations and the Fed does not raise interest rates at its next FOMC meeting, wider macro factors could still affect sentiment. In other words, a positive inflation reading may not be enough to turn the market bullish in December.

This leaves crypto at risk of recording its worst Q4 performances on record.

Sticky inflation, rising oil prices and a stronger dollar could keep pressure on crypto.

Even if inflation meets expectations, broader macro risks could prevent a December recovery and deepen Q4 losses.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

XRP’s price action may be frustrating investors, but popular crypto analyst Dan Gambardello believes the current market turmoil could be hiding a much bigger opportunity.

While warning that repeated manipulation is keeping the Ripple-linked crypto trapped in a cycle of familiar price movements, Gambardello maintains that the broader crypto market is eventually heading toward an explosive bull run. His latest assessment raises questions about how long XRP holders may have to endure the current market games before bullish momentum finally takes over.

In a recent development, in his latest commentary, Dan Gambardello pointed to XRP’s hourly price chart as evidence of what he considers repeated market manipulation. According to him, the token’s short-term price movements have become increasingly predictable, with similar patterns playing out repeatedly rather than allowing a sustained directional move to develop.

It has been revealed that describing the situation as a case of “rinse and repeat,” the analyst suggested that market participants are dealing with recurring price tactics that continue to frustrate XRP traders. This pattern, in his view, reflects the challenging conditions crypto investors face as they wait for broader bullish momentum to return.

Gambardello’s remarks come on the heels of XRP’s notable rebound on November 23, when the cryptocurrency briefly reclaimed the $1 mark after enduring several consecutive sessions of downward pressure.

It has been revealed that the rally initially gathered momentum from around $0.94, with buyers pushing XRP toward $0.99 before a fresh wave of buying lifted it above $1.02. However, the upward momentum quickly faded. XRP struggled to hold above the psychological $1 threshold as renewed selling pressure dragged the token toward $0.95 within hours. At press time, XRP had slipped to approximately $0.9176, marking a 10.04% drop from its intraday peak of $1.02.

Notably, his warning about XRP’s current price behavior does not undermine his longer-term optimism.

Despite his concerns about XRP’s recent market movements, Gambardello remains firmly optimistic about the crypto market’s long-term prospects. He believes the industry is eventually heading toward a meteoric bull market that could launch a powerful rally across digital assets.

According to recent reports, the pundit’s outlook suggests that the current wave of volatility and alleged market manipulation should not be mistaken for the end of the broader bullish opportunity. While investors may have to contend with repeated price swings and frustrating market conditions in the near term, he expects the crypto market to eventually regain momentum and deliver a much stronger upside move.

For XRP holders, this presents an interesting contrast between the token’s current struggles and the analyst’s longer-term expectations. Nonetheless, Gambardello has not provided a specific timeline or price target for when the anticipated bull run could commence.

Volkswagen is turning one of its best-selling nameplates into an electric SUV. The fresh ID. Tiguan is now rolling off the assembly line and will replace the ID.4 in 2027.

It has been revealed that the ID.4 and ID.5 are on the way out, and the fresh ID. Tiguan will replace them in Volkswagen’s EV lineup next year.

Sources indicate that following the ID. Polo and ID. Cross, which are now on sale in Europe, the ID. Tiguan is the next model to go on sale as a “True Volkswagen,” as the organization calls it.

The fresh electric SUV adopts Volkswagen’s best-selling nameplate, the Tiguan, as part of its shift away from the numerical system used on the outgoing ID.4 and ID.5.

Volkswagen announced on Thursday that series production of the electric ID. Tiguan has now begun at its Embden Plant in Germany.

“The Tiguan is our best-selling model worldwide, and the ID.4 and ID.5 are among our most successful electric cars,” VW Brand CEO Thomas Shafer said last month after unveiling the fresh SUV. He added that “The ID. Tiguan brings these two success stories together.”.

The ID. Tiguan will be a step change from its predecessors, the ID.4 and ID.5, featuring Volkswagen’s “Pure Positive” design language, which includes an overhauled interior and exterior design and updated tech.

Recent findings suggest that volkswagen noted the ID. Tiguan’s “hallmark feature” is the completely redesigned exterior. The new design remains closer to the gas-powered Tiguan, with a boxy, traditional SUV look.

According to recent reports, unlike the ID.4’s aerodynamic design, the newly introduced ID. Tiguan features a wide, chunky front end and traditional pull-style door handles instead of the flush ones.

In Volkswagen’s words, the new ID. Tiguan electric SUV “looks like a vehicle from the premium segment.”.

Inside, the updates are just as evident. The overhauled interior features Volkswagen’s newly introduced infotainment setup, including a 10″ Digital Cockpit and a 15″ center display. There’s also an optional 12″ passenger screen available.

It has been revealed that another highlight is the return of physical buttons. After listening to customer feedback from current drivers, Volkswagen added physical buttons under the center display and on the steering wheel for climate control and other vehicle functions.

To spark a bit of nostalgia, VW added a fun fresh Retro Mode feature that transforms the Digital Cockpit and center display to mimic the style of iconic models like the first-generation Golf.

Drivers can also choose from six classic VW models to display in a virtual “garage” on the infotainment screen: Golf I, Golf II Country, Golf IV, Tiguan I, Race Touareg, and Beetle.

The new Volkswagen ID. Tiguan will be available with two battery packs and three performance levels:.

Industry observers note that depending on the configuration, the ID. Tiguan offers a “fresh benchmark” for Volkswagen’s electric SUVs in Europe with a WLTP range of up to 377 miles (607 km).

Industry observers note that volkswagen opened orders for the ID. Tiguan in Germany and a few other European markets in October, starting at €42,695 ($47,800). It’s available in three trims: Trend, Life, and Style.

After it launches in Europe through early 2027, Volkswagen noted the ID. Tiguan will go on sale in North America to replace the ID.4.

Apparently, the fresh ID Tiguan has a slightly better Cx (Drag Coefficient) at 0.26 versus 0.28 on first gen ID4 and 0.27 on 2nd gen. According to VW, it’s achieved using front air curtains, a minimal air intake, an enclosed underbody, and a longer roof spoiler.

Volkswagen stated prices and other details will come in “due course.” The current VW ID.4 uses an 82 kWh battery that provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 291 miles in the RWD version. The AWD model offers around 263 miles.

Since the European model offers close to 25 miles (40 km) more WLTP range than the outgoing ID.4, the ID. Tiguan is expected to offer over 300 miles on the EPA scale.

Official US prices have not yet been announced. The outgoing ID.4 has a starting MSRP of about $45,000, so the ID. Tiguan will likely be priced similarly.

NYSE’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily rule out XRP.

The New York Stock Exchange’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily shut out XRP, wealth commentator Kamilah Stevenson argues in her latest video.

Her distinction: settling share ownership and moving money across currencies are separate jobs, and winning one does not automatically secure the other.

According to Dr. Stevenson, Ava Labs announced that Avalanche would provide the core ledger for the clearing firm behind the proposed platform.

She cites Wall Street Journal reporting that Avalanche would be its sole settlement blockchain, with regulatory approval still required.

Industry observers note that the proposed venue would support around-the-clock trading and near-instant settlement. Stevenson states NYSE tested Avalanche for roughly a year, prioritizing transaction speed, predictable costs and control over who can participate.

That permissioning capability matters for a regulated exchange. Avalanche (AVAX) can support customized networks with participation restrictions, rather than requiring the exchange to conduct settlement on an unrestricted public network.

Sources indicate that AVAX rose as much as roughly 10% on the news, according to the video. Stevenson, who discloses holding the token, calls the selection a win for Avalanche, but cautions against treating infrastructure adoption as proof of investment returns.

It has been revealed that “A network being used by a massive name and its token being needed” are different things, she states. The announcement, in her account, provided neither revenue figures nor a commitment that NYSE would buy or hold AVAX.

In a recent development, dr. Stevenson’s XRP thesis centers on overseas investors funding dollar-denominated stock purchases outside conventional banking hours.

Sources indicate that A trader holding yen or another currency would need access to dollars or dollar-linked funding before buying U.S. shares.

Industry observers note that she argues that this creates an opportunity for cross-border payment infrastructure, including XRP. But it remains a proposed use case, not a disclosed partnership: “I’m not telling you that NYSE is going to pick XRP for that.”.

Sources indicate that the YouTube video episode does not establish that XRP would be necessary for such funding. Nor does expanded trading access, by itself, demonstrate future demand for the token.

Dr. Kamilah Stevenson also states the platform would support tokenized stocks issued across multiple blockchains, distinguishing asset issuance from the ledger used for settlement.

Those details matter more than a simple Avalanche-versus-XRP contest: the unresolved questions are which services institutions actually adopt, what generates revenue, and whether that activity requires either token.

BYD rolled out the Denza N8 EV in China, a five-seat luxury SUV that promises more than 1,000 km (621 miles) of CLTC range, a tech-filled cabin, and plenty of premium extras.

It has been revealed that another day, another newly introduced BYD vehicle is now on sale in China. After opening preorders for the Denza N8 EV a few weeks ago, BYD held the grand launch event on Thursday.

The upcoming N8 EV, or “the king of large 5-seater pure electric vehicles,” as Denza called it, is available in six variants, including four battery-electric (EV) and two plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrain options.

The all-electric Denza N8 starts at 269,900 yuan, or about $40,500, with prices ranging up to 329,900 yuan ($49,500) for the Flagship model. The PHEV models start at 300,900 yuan and 32,900 yuan, respectively.

Measuring 5,150 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,820 mm high, with a 3,075 mm wheelbase, the Denza N8 EV is slightly longer than the Kia EV9 and Hyundai IONIQ 9.

Inside, the interior is pretty over the top with a huge 30″ panoramic infotainment screen that stretches nearly the entire passenger-side dashboard. There’s also a newly introduced 43″ (1.1 meter) panoramic head-up display (PHUD) at the bottom of the windshield.

BYD added a few premium extras like front and rear zero-gravity seats, a drop-down ceiling entertainment screen, ambient lighting, and wireless phone chargers.

The Denza N8 is offered with a single rear-wheel-drive (RWD) or a tri-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain. The RWD variant uses a single motor that delivers either 320 kW (429 hp) or 370 kW (496 hp), depending on the configuration.

The tri-motor Denza N8 debuts BYD’s e3 Evo technology. The setup includes three electric motors: a 270 kW (362 hp) front motor and two 310 kW (416 hp) rear motors, for a combined output of 890 kW (1,193 hp).

BYD’s Denza said the N8 EV boasts an all-electric CLTC range of 1,003 km (623 miles), “making it the world’s longest-range mass-produced all-electric SUV.”.

To put it in perspective, that’s as much as the outgoing N8 plug-in hybrid (PHEV) it’s replacing, which offered a combined CLTC range of 1,003 km (623 miles) on a full tank of gas and a full charge.

It’s available with two second-gen BYD Blade battery packs: 105.792 kWh and 130.15 kWh, delivering CLTC ranges of up to 885 km (549 miles) and 1,003 km (623 miles).

In a recent development, with BYD’s second-gen Blade Batteries and Flash Charging tech, the Denza N8 EV can charge from 10% to 70% in five minutes. Charging from 10% to 97% takes just nine minutes.

Like many of its upcoming luxury vehicles, the Denza N8 is equipped with BYD’s premium tech and features, such as its DiSus-A intelligent air suspension system and God’s Eye 5.0 intelligent driving assistance system.

BYD also sells the extended Denza N8L in China, which went on sale earlier this year, starting at 299,800 yuan ($45,000).

In October, the total XRP that flowed into exchanges throughout the month was estimated at around 6 billion XRP, suggesting that XRP selling pressure has eased compared with the previous month.

This has drawn attention across the crypto market as the price of XRP suffered larger losses this month compared with last month, sparking questions about whether investor confidence is recovering.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CleanSpark has begun selling Bitcoin from its treasury to finance acquisitions as the company accelerates its expansion into artificial intelligence infrastructure.

In a recent development, during the company's Nov. 24 earnings call, President and CFO Gary Vecchiarelli said CleanSpark had sold some of its Bitcoin holdings since the end of September to strengthen its cash position ahead of anticipated acquisitions.

“We've sold some Bitcoin to pad the balance sheet with cash to prepare for some acquisitions that we expect to make in the near future.”.

In a recent development, vecchiarelli added that CleanSpark could sell additional Bitcoin or borrow against its holdings to finance acquisitions without diluting existing shareholders. The company also intends to sell virtually all newly mined Bitcoin to fund daily operations.

CleanSpark ended September with approximately $1.3 billion in reported liquidity, comprising $204.8 million in cash and cash equivalents and approximately $1.13 billion in Bitcoin holdings and related exposure.

The tech giant reported exposure equivalent to 13,530 BTC at fiscal year-end but has not disclosed how much Bitcoin it subsequently sold.

The treasury strategy comes as deteriorating Bitcoin mining economics weigh on CleanSpark's financial performance.

According to its fiscal 2026 results, annual revenue declined 25% to $576.5 million, while the tech giant recorded a net loss of $987.1 million, compared with net income of $364 million a year earlier.

Vecchiarelli attributed approximately two-thirds of the earnings reversal to noncash adjustments in the value of its Bitcoin holdings.

Industry observers note that however, profitability also deteriorated across its mining operations. Annual gross margins contracted from 55% to 41% as the average value of mined Bitcoin fell from approximately $97,600 to $79,500.

The decline occurred despite improvements in fleet efficiency and a reduction in electricity costs from $0.057 to $0.055 per kilowatt-hour.

Against this backdrop, CleanSpark is directing more capital toward AI data centers and acquiring land and power infrastructure.

The firm secured a 20-year, $6.6 billion lease with an investment-grade tenant at its Sandersville facility in Georgia and raised $2.276 billion through secured notes to fully fund the project's development. It also expanded its Texas infrastructure portfolio through acquisitions supporting up to 885 MW of power capacity.

Vecchiarelli noted management sees further acquisition opportunities as a better use of available capital than repurchasing CleanSpark shares, despite believing its stock is undervalued.

While Bitcoin provides CleanSpark with an alternative to equity financing, the cryptocurrency's recent decline has reduced the collateral value supporting its existing borrowing.

Industry observers note that cleanSpark's annual filing demonstrated that it had borrowed $90 million through a $100 million revolving credit facility with Two Prime Lending as of Sept. 30.

The company pledged 1,665 BTC worth $139.1 million at the time, giving the loan a loan-to-value ratio of approximately 65%.

Sources indicate that under the agreement, a ratio exceeding 74% triggers a margin call, while liquidation can occur above 80%. Based on the September loan balance and collateral, those thresholds correspond to Bitcoin prices of approximately $73,046 and $67,568, respectively.

Sources indicate that with Bitcoin trading near $59,000 on Nov. 25, the same collateral would be worth approximately $98.2 million, pushing the loan-to-value ratio to nearly 92% if the position remained unchanged.

Industry observers note that the miner reported $90 million outstanding and 1,665 BTC pledged to Two Prime at Sept. 30.

As Bitcoin falls, the same loan balance takes up a larger share of the pledged coins’ value.

According to recent reports, the illustration holds Sept. 30 principal and pledged coins fixed. The current debt balance, pledged coin count, lender valuation and any lender action remain unknown.

Industry observers note that loan-to-value is principal divided by collateral value. The reported Sept. 30 ratio uses $139.128 million in collateral. Each boundary price is $90 million divided by the product of 1,665 BTC and the threshold ratio. The $59,000 case values the collateral at 1,665 × $59,000. Prices are rounded to dollars and ratios to whole percentages.

In a recent development, the illustration holds Sept. 30 principal and pledged coins fixed. The current debt balance, pledged coin count, lender valuation and any lender action remain unknown.

CleanSpark has not disclosed whether it has subsequently increased its collateral or reduced its outstanding debt.

Shareholders will also have less frequent visibility into those decisions after CleanSpark discontinued monthly operational updates in favor of quarterly reporting.

Its next quarterly disclosure could reveal how much of its Bitcoin treasury the company has committed to financing its AI expansion and whether additional acquisitions will require further sales or borrowing.

Bitcoin ETFs shed $4 billion — How did one fund hide the cracks before leading the exit?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2013 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that U.S Spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $4.14 billion over three weeks, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for roughly 84% of the withdrawals.
  • It has been revealed that in the week leading up to October 19, U.S Spot Bitcoin ETFs appeared to be doing rather well.
  • Recent findings suggest that there was one small complication, though.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that U.S Spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $4.14 billion over three weeks, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for roughly 84% of the withdrawals. However, the same fund had been concealing weakness elsewhere just weeks ago. The story behind the numbers is considerably more complicated than the headline.

It has been revealed that in the week leading up to October 19, U.S Spot Bitcoin ETFs appeared to be doing rather well. The funds collectively attracted $301.2 million in net inflows. That’s quite a reassuring development for a market that had become accustomed to treating ETF demand as a barometer of Bitcoin’s institutional appeal.

Recent findings suggest that there was one small complication, though. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) had brought in $565.7 million on its own. Every other fund combined lost $264.5 million. So, how healthy was that $301.2 million gain if it depended entirely on one fund?

Three weeks later, the answer became harder to ignore.

Between November 2 and 20, Bitcoin ETFs suffered a staggering $4.14 billion in net withdrawals, according to Farside Investors. By the way, IBIT ALONE accounted for approximately $3.49 billion, or 84% of the exodus.

And the selling gathered pace as the week wore on. Nearly $1.79 billion left in the final week, around 1.7 times the previous week’s withdrawals. From November 17 through November 20, each trading session ended with a larger outflow than the previous one.

October’s biggest source of support had become November’s biggest source of pressure. The reversal was striking enough. In fact, what was happening beneath it was more revealing!

BlackRock’s influence on the industry’s performance was hardly a one-week curiosity.

Industry observers note that the pattern continued into October 26–30. IBIT attracted another $176.9 million while competing funds collectively lost $379.3 million. Even though the industry finished that week in the red, BlackRock’s inflows effectively absorbed nearly half the damage.

Then, on October 30, the reprieve ended.

Recent findings suggest that spot BTC ETFs recorded roughly $643 million in withdrawals in a single session, with IBIT contributing approximately $234 million. The fund that had been cushioning the industry’s losses was now participating in them.

November made that reversal unmistakable.

Industry observers note that IBIT accounted for approximately 94% of the industry’s net outflows during the first week, 85% during the second, and 76% during the third. Curiously, its share declined even as the third week brought the industry’s biggest outflow yet.

In a recent development, that was the more consequential development. Other funds, including Fidelity’s FBTC and products from Grayscale and ARK, were contributing increasingly to the selling. What had initially been concentrated overwhelmingly in BlackRock’s product was beginning to spread.

A market once held up by its largest fund was now being dragged down by it, with competitors increasingly joining the retreat.

Now, IBIT was already by far the industry’s biggest fund. Perhaps its dominance in the withdrawals was simply a consequence of its size. Hence why that possibility deserved a closer look. However, a closer look at this position revealed another complication.

In a recent development, A fund holding most of the industry’s assets will naturally account for a significant share of its movements. A billion dollars leaving a $60 billion product is hardly equivalent to the same amount leaving one worth $5 billion.

Industry observers note that by October 30, IBIT held approximately $62.7 billion in Bitcoin, according to iShares holdings data. Looking at it broadly, the Bitcoin ETF market held roughly $98.14 billion, based on SoSoValue.

BlackRock therefore controlled about two-thirds of the industry’s assets entering November. And yet, it accounted for 84% of the subsequent three-week net withdrawals.

The disparity only becomes sharper when adjusted for size.

According to recent reports, IBIT’s $3.49 billion outflow was equivalent to approximately 5.6% of its starting holdings value. For all the other funds combined, the equivalent was just 1.8%.

Sources indicate that in relative terms, BlackRock’s fund experienced roughly three times the withdrawal pressure of its competitors. Its scale explained part of its dominance, but hardly all of it.

Recent findings suggest that the underlying Bitcoin inventory tells a similar story. IBIT held approximately 811,817 BTC on October 30. By November 20, that had fallen to roughly 760,926 BTC, a reduction of nearly 50,900 BTC or 6.3%.

Bitcoin’s declining price could reduce the dollar value of those holdings, but it could not account for the disappearance of the coins themselves. IBIT’s inventory had genuinely contracted.

In a recent development, the departures were measurable. The identities of those departing were another matter.

Sources indicate that A $4 billion ETF outflow makes it tempting to declare that institutional investors are abandoning Bitcoin. Yet the available data cannot distinguish an asset manager reducing exposure from an individual investor selling shares, or a market participant unwinding a hedged position.

In a recent development, nor does it establish whether the capital left Bitcoin altogether or found another route back into the market. That uncertainty matters because the industry has grown comfortable treating ETF inflows as evidence of institutional conviction. Applying the opposite interpretation to withdrawals may be tempting, but it is no more conclusive.

What November demonstrated was a substantial withdrawal of capital from these investment products, led disproportionately by BlackRock’s IBIT.

Whether it represented a broader loss of faith in Bitcoin was a considerably larger question though.

And while investors were heading for the exits, there seemed to be little indication that the fund itself had stopped functioning as intended.

There is an understandable tendency to interpret large ETF outflows as a sign that the investment product itself has somehow failed. However, IBIT’s trading data tells us a more measured story.

In a recent development, according to iShares, IBIT closed at $33.02 on November 20 against a net asset value of $33.05, a discount of about 0.10%. Its 30-day median bid-ask spread was 0.02%. In other words, the fund traded almost exactly at the value of the Bitcoin it holds, even as markets were falling.

According to recent reports, trading was heavy. About 109.2 million IBIT shares changed hands on November 20, more than twice the fund’s 30-day average of about 50.1 million.

It has been revealed that that is not the same as money leaving the fund though because trading volume is not net flow. A 30-day median spread also doesn’t show that trading stayed cheap at every volatile moment.

Still, nothing here suggests investors were fleeing a broken product. They were trading a working fund whose underlying asset had dropped sharply. IBIT’s NAV fell $2.08 (5.92%) on November 20 to $33.05, and its NAV total return for 2026 stood at −29.06% as of November 19.

Wall Street made Bitcoin easier to buy. That was never the same promise as making it safer to hold. That distinction matters for the question that comes next — how much of the fall in ETF assets was money leaving, and how much was the price?

According to SoSoValue, combined Spot Bitcoin ETF assets reached approximately $110.8 billion on October 5. By November 20, they had fallen to roughly $71.3 billion.

A decline approaching $39.5 billion sounds extraordinary beside three weeks of approximately $4.14 billion in net withdrawals.

However, assets under management represent the market value of what these funds hold. That value changes both when investors create or redeem shares and when Bitcoin itself rises or falls.

Recent findings suggest that using Coinbase Bitcoin prices recorded by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, Bitcoin fell from approximately $85,821 on October 5 to $58,831 on November 20 — A fall of 31.4%.

Over the same period, reported ETF assets fell by approximately 36%.

In a recent development, such a comparison strongly suggests that Bitcoin’s price decline accounted for much of the reduction in ETF asset values. It is not a precise decomposition — flows occurred throughout the period, holdings changed, and the dates and valuation methodologies must be matched before assigning an exact proportion to each driver.

Still, the broad conclusion is difficult to miss.

Tens of billions of dollars can disappear from reported fund asset values without an equivalent sum being withdrawn by investors. A falling portfolio value and a redeemed investment are two different financial events. Treating them interchangeably gives a dramatic headline considerably more authority than it deserves.

Bitcoin’s ETF market was not the only place seeing withdrawals either.

From November 9 to 13, U.S Spot Ether ETFs lost about $398.9 million, according to Farside. BlackRock’s iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA) accounted for about $311.1 million of that, or 78%. The following week, Ether funds lost about $306 million, with ETHA responsible for about $230 million or 75%.

That’s the same pattern we saw in Bitcoin — one BlackRock fund carrying most of the headline outflow.

Stablecoins told a slower story. According to DefiLlama, their combined market capitalisation was about $295.3 billion on October 30. It fell to $290.2 billion by November 6, $285.6 billion by November 13, and $281.3 billion by November 20. That is a contraction of about $14 billion, or 4.8%, in three weeks.

Unlike the ETF flows, which peaked in the final week, stablecoins shrank at a fairly steady pace — about $5.1 billion, $4.6 billion, then $4.3 billion a week.

Stablecoins are the dollar-pegged tokens traders use for settlement, trading balances, and collateral. So, a falling supply suggests liquidity may be tightening beyond the regulated ETF market. The two trends overlapped, but they moved at different speeds.

Bitcoin’s own trading schedule adds a complication too.

FRED’s Coinbase series showed Bitcoin falling from about $68,178 on November 13 to $62,891 on November 14, a drop of 7.8%, after that week’s ETF sessions ended.

In a recent development, however, after the much heavier withdrawal week ending November 20, Bitcoin went the other way. It fell from about $58,831 on November 20 to $60,992 on November 22 — A gain of 3.7%.

Sources indicate that two weekends prove nothing on their own, and FRED’s prices are taken at 5 p.m Pacific, not at the ETF close. But they do show that a record ETF outflow and a falling price don’t move in lockstep.

There is no need to minimise the withdrawals. About $4.14 billion in three weeks is a major reversal, particularly when the final week was the worst of the three.

It has been revealed that nor should IBIT’s concentration be brushed off as a consequence of its size. Its 84% share of the net outflows exceeded its roughly two-thirds share of starting industry assets.

However, context changes the interpretation.

SoSoValue’s November 20 figures still showed about $52.8 billion in cumulative net inflows since January 2024. That is down roughly $4 billion from where November began, but nearly three years of accumulated inflows were not erased by three difficult weeks.

October offers a useful warning about reading any headline in isolation. The same fund that masked withdrawals elsewhere in two October weeks went on to account for most of November’s exits. The industry totals recorded both developments accurately, yet told very different stories depending on whether you looked at the funds behind them.

It has been revealed that the ETF structure broadened access to Bitcoin. It also gave investors a familiar, liquid way to reduce exposure. Neither is a guarantee about Bitcoin’s price.

Recent findings suggest that perhaps institutions were cutting risk. Or, retail investors may have been heading for the exits. Others could simply have been unwinding complex positions that had little to do with long-term conviction in Bitcoin. All three are plausible explanations.

What they do establish is narrower but more useful — the withdrawals were substantial, heavily concentrated in one product, and increasingly shared across competing funds as November went on.

So, the next time a billion-dollar ETF outflow makes the headlines, the interesting questions begin after the headline. Which funds accounted for it? How large were the withdrawals relative to their assets? Is the number money leaving a product, or is the market value of its holdings falling?

And one more, which no flow table can answer — Who was actually selling?

Institutional progress continues, but the development of Ripple’s custody service doesn’t spark up a rally.

XRP’s price briefly climbed above $1 this week, reaching roughly $1.03 before sellers pushed it back below the level within hours. The move followed a rebound from near $0.91, leaving the token trading around $0.93 to $0.96.

Recent findings suggest that the push above $1 was helped in part by traders closing bearish futures positions. XRP short liquidations made up a substantial share of recent XRP futures liquidations, a dynamic that can produce sharp rallies without durable buying.

According to recent reports, spot-market data has shown sellers retaining the upper hand in recent weeks, though the pace of net selling has eased. Large crypto holders accumulated an estimated $72 million in XRP over several days, standing apart from reported selling in Bitcoin and Ether (ETH).

That activity has not yet turned $1 from resistance into a reliable floor. XRP was rejected around the level more than once during the latest stretch of trading.

The price weakness has continued even as Ripple expands its institutional footprint. Yapı Kredi, one of Türkiye’s largest private banks, intends to use Ripple Custody for digital-asset services connected to its crypto platform, with the infrastructure operated on the bank’s own premises.

According to recent reports, ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin has also grown. Its circulating supply recently reached a high near $2.87 billion, briefly overtaking USD1 before subsequent redemptions put the rival token marginally back ahead.

In a recent development, 💵 Ripple's RLUSD has overtaken Trump-linked USD1 by circulating supply, hitting a record $2.87B. Ripple's stablecoin keeps growing, even in a bear market. The onchain dollar keeps growing. This is where real adoption is happening.#RLUSD #Ripple #Stablecoins.

About $761 million of RLUSD supply is held on the XRP Ledger, where XRP is used to pay transaction fees.

Those developments strengthen Ripple’s broader payments, custody and stablecoin business, but they do not automatically create immediate buying pressure for XRP.

Turkish XRP trading against the lira, for example, has fallen sharply from year-earlier levels despite the bank custody announcement.

In a recent development, XRP’s price has lost about 26% over the past month and remains well below its longer-term trend averages. The altcoin now trades just one cent above the low-tier Bollinger Band (BOLL).

A break above the recent high near $1.03 could bring the $1.04 to $1.08 area into view, while failure to hold the $0.91 to $0.92 support zone could expose $0.86.

Ripple’s institutional progress may matter over a longer horizon, but XRP investors are still waiting for that momentum to show up decisively in the market.

Morgan Stanley has disclosed its latest crypto-related holdings in a quarterly Form 13F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. According to the filing, the bank's U.S. equity portfolio was valued at around $1.96 trillion as of Sept. 30, up from $1.89 trillion at the end of June.

Most of the crypto-related positions in the filing are Bitcoin products and Bitcoin-linked stocks, and the bank also reported a small amount of XRP exposure through three spot exchange-traded funds.

The largest crypto-related position in the filing is Strategy (MSTR). Morgan Stanley held around 10.88 million MSTR shares worth about $1.67 billion at the end of September, up from 9.33 million shares at the end of the second quarter.

Industry observers note that the bank also increased its position in BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) from 16.48 million to 19.52 million shares, and the IBIT stake was worth about $924 million as of Sept. 30.

According to recent reports, besides, Morgan Stanley reported 6.72 million units of its own Morgan Stanley Bitcoin Trust (MSBT), up from 2.57 million units at the end of June. In the second-quarter filing, the MSBT position was worth about $43.3 million. MSBT started trading on NYSE Arca in April, and it was the first spot Bitcoin ETF issued by a major U.S. bank.

Among crypto stocks, Morgan Stanley also held around 10.54 million Robinhood (HOOD) shares worth about $1.19 billion and 3.72 million Coinbase (COIN) shares worth about $694 million.

Industry observers note that morgan Stanley reported $116,097 in XRP ETF holdings as of Sept. 30. Franklin's XRP fund accounted for $111,885 of that amount, REX-Osprey's fund for $3,098, and the Bitwise XRP ETF for the remaining $1,114.

According to recent reports, the bank held the same three funds at the end of June. In the second quarter, Morgan Stanley reported 6,715 shares of the Franklin fund, 255 shares of the REX-Osprey fund and 67 shares of the Bitwise fund. Before that, the bank's first-quarter filing showed 1,700 shares of the Volatility Shares XRP ETF and 100 shares of the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF worth $15,488 in total.

On Wednesday, XRP was trading at around $0.908, down 2.23% over 24 hours, according to CoinMarketCap.

It has been revealed that morgan Stanley was one of seven banks that disclosed XRP-linked ETF holdings in third-quarter 13F filings. The positions of the seven banks totaled about $29.4 million as of Sept. 30, and Italy's Intesa Sanpaolo accounted for $27.21 million of that amount.

It has been revealed that goldman Sachs reported much larger XRP positions. The bank's XRP ETF holdings rose from $87 million in the second quarter to $144 million in the third quarter, and Goldman's crypto portfolio was worth around $2.64 billion in total.

XRP has been part of crypto’s story for more than a decade, through every cycle, and it’s still helping shape what comes next. We’re grateful to everyone who’s been part of the journey so far. Here’s to year two!

The timing is particularly interesting here.

Recent findings suggest that bitwise’s report comes as XRP’s technical and on-chain metrics continue to deteriorate. Meanwhile, prediction markets are also increasingly pricing in a year-end target below $0.80. Against this backdrop, the key question is whether Bitwise’s report can strengthen institutional interest and turn the current bearish setup into a bear trap.

The impact of Bitwise’s one-year XRP ETF performance could already be triggering FOMO.

In a recent development, notably, another Wall Street firm has disclosed exposure to an XRP ETF. Atlanta-based Arkadios Wealth Advisors, which looks after $8.79 billion in client assets, stated this in its most recent SEC document.

According to recent reports, the key takeaway? XRP’s derivatives continue to be significantly net short, with the long/short ratio showing a pronounced sell-side sentiment. Interestingly, however, the XRP/BTC ratio has risen by almost 5% following three successive weeks of upside.

In essence, broader market weakness could create room for more capital to flow into XRP.

This makes it an important setup to watch over the coming months. The logic is simple —  Entering Q4, market participants are already factoring in further downside potential. In this context, Bitwise’s recent report, growing ETF exposure, and Ripple’s expansion in Turkiye could encourage further capital rotation into XRP.

If this trend continues, XRP’s ongoing consolidation around $0.90 could turn out to be an accumulation phase before a potential bear trap.

Bitwise’s XRP ETF has attracted $667 million in net inflows, while growing institutional exposure and Ripple’s expansion in Turkiye point to sustained demand.

  • The electric SUV has played a major part in Kia’s turnaround in China and is among the top-selling EVs in places like Australia.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kia isn’t wasting any time updating its Sportage-sized EV5 electric SUV. Leaked images just gave us our first look at what’s changing.

Recent findings suggest that while Kia doesn’t sell the EV5 in the US, the electric SUV has been a hit in other global markets. It first went on sale in China in 2023, and Kia launched the global model last year; it is now available in Europe, Canada, the UK, and other overseas regions.

The electric SUV has played a major part in Kia’s turnaround in China and is among the top-selling EVs in places like Australia.

Recent findings suggest that kia is already preparing to introduce an updated version in 2027. The updated EV5 was revealed through Australian Design Rule (ADR) regulatory documents, including images of the new version and some powertrain specs.

Front- and all-wheel-drive variants will get a power boost with up to 234 hp (175 kW) in FWD and 334 hp (249 kW) for AWD models.

The new EV5 will still use the same 64.2 kWh and 88.1 kWh battery packs, but updated range figures have yet to be unveiled.

Kia’s current model offers a WLTP range of up to 248 miles (400 km) from the smaller battery and 345 miles (555 km) from the larger battery.

As previous spy images have shown, the updated Kia EV5 features a few slight exterior design changes.

These changes include upcoming front and rear bumpers, similar to those of the rugged EV5 WKNDR Concept Kia revealed last November at the Guangzhou Motor Show.

A post shared by SHORTS CAR (@shorts_car).

Recent findings suggest that saying there are updates with no context is borderline useless. A power boost from what? The EV5 isn't in the US, so I don't have its looks anywhere close to memorized.

It has been revealed that hopefully the power increase is more than just a software update, having hardware updates for better efficiency/lower weight/lower costs even if they're not passed on to consumers. If they're updating the looks, they should coincide with better aerodynamics for better higher speed range and efficiency.

Recent spy photos in Korea from ShortsCar revealed the EV5 upgrade features a 27″ center infotainment screen, similar to the Hyundai Elexio and Kia Seltos that are made in China.

A sticker on the back said the vehicle was destined for the Philippines, meaning it’s the EV5 that’s produced in China.

Since Kia introduced the China-made EV5 in 2023, it’s due for a refresh around 2027. Whether and when Kia will introduce the updated global version, which is produced in Korea, has yet to be confirmed.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ripple has partnered with Turkish banking giant Yapı Kredi to provide digital asset custody infrastructure for its cryptocurrency business.
  • 25 statement, Yapı Kredi mentioned it has deployed Ripple Custody within its own infrastructure to safeguard digital assets held through Yapı Kredi Kripto, its cryptocurrency trading platform.
  • The partnership expands Ripple's presence in Türkiye, where financial institutions are increasingly developing regulated digital asset services.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ripple has partnered with Turkish banking giant Yapı Kredi to provide digital asset custody infrastructure for its cryptocurrency business.

In a recent development, in a Nov. 25 statement, Yapı Kredi mentioned it has deployed Ripple Custody within its own infrastructure to safeguard digital assets held through Yapı Kredi Kripto, its cryptocurrency trading platform.

The partnership expands Ripple's presence in Türkiye, where financial institutions are increasingly developing regulated digital asset services.

Yapı Kredi is one of the country's largest private banks, with total assets of 4.4 trillion Turkish lira as of September. The lender operates 723 branches nationwide and employs more than 14,000 people.

The bank already facilitates round-the-clock lira transfers between its customers' bank accounts and cryptocurrency exchanges BtcTurk and Paribu.

Ripple disclosed an on-site custody deployment at Yapı Kredi. Garanti BBVA Kripto publishes active XRP trading and withdrawal statuses.

Customers need a lira funding route, an XRP buy option and a way to move XRP off the platform.

Recent findings suggest that garanti’s lira instruction covers account activation. Its public withdrawal status omits the network. The diagram compares published service details as of Nov. 25.

Industry observers note that compare public bank and platform materials checked on Nov. 25, 2026. Filled points show published features or status. The separate activation point identifies a bank-transfer step whose documented purpose is account activation. Hollow points mark unconfirmed retail steps.

Garanti’s lira instruction covers account activation. Its public withdrawal status omits the network. The diagram compares published service details as of Nov. 25.

However, Yapı Kredi has been developing infrastructure to offer cryptocurrency services through its own subsidiary.

In October, Yapı Kredi Kripto selected financial technology provider Integral to support digital asset trading, complementing the custody infrastructure it has now secured through Ripple.

Eylem Karaca, an executive at Yapı Kredi Technology, mentioned:.

“As digital assets become an increasingly key part of the financial ecosystem, we're focused on building the secure, reliable infrastructure needed to support this evolution.”.

The partnership comes as Türkiye's regulatory framework creates commercial opportunities for institutional cryptocurrency custody providers.

Under rules introduced by the country's Capital Markets Board, cryptocurrency trading platforms must hold at least 95% of customer digital assets with authorized custodians.

Ripple remarked it is the only custody technology provider working with Türkiye's major licensed bank-based crypto custodians, positioning the company to benefit from traditional financial institutions entering the market.

Türkiye ranks among the world's ten largest retail cryptocurrency markets, according to TRM Labs, with demand supported by persistent lira depreciation and interest in alternative savings instruments.

Ripple also identified XRP as one of the country's most widely held digital assets.

The manufacturer previously partnered with Garanti BBVA Kripto and IBM in October 2024 to strengthen the custody infrastructure supporting the bank-backed cryptocurrency platform.

Garanti BBVA Kripto served more than 14,000 people at the time and offered services involving Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, and several other digital assets.

The platform now supports direct XRP trading against the Turkish lira, alongside XRP deposits and withdrawals.

Yapı Kredi has yet to disclose its retail launch date or the cryptocurrencies it supports. A similar offering would give Turkish investors another bank-backed channel to buy and hold XRP.

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, french senators on Nov.
  • It has been revealed that they would have had to report those assets as of Dec.
  • This would have been the case even if they had held the same coins since January without making any sales.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, french senators on Nov. 24 rejected a proposal that would have required taxpayers to disclose self-hosted cryptocurrency holdings exceeding €100,000.

It has been revealed that they would have had to report those assets as of Dec. 31.

This would have been the case even if they had held the same coins since January without making any sales.

Two matching amendments to the French 2027 budget were rejected by the Senate during the first reading of the draft.

Senators Pascal Savoldelli and Anne-Sophie Romagny reintroduced the proposal after it briefly passed in the National Assembly earlier in the month.

French taxpayers must disclose their crypto assets held on foreign crypto platforms.

Industry observers note that these amendments would have expanded disclosure requirements to wallets that owners directly control. This pertains to a wallet that is not managed by an exchange or another custodian.

Sources indicate that the French National Assembly approved the €100,000 disclosure threshold in a 150-44 vote on Nov. 3. There were also eight abstentions.

The next day, the National Assembly voted down the entire revenue portion of the budget.

This vote brought down the wallet disclosure provision along with the rest of the budget.

However, the subsequent effort to revive the provision in the Senate was defeated.

It should be noted that the 2027 budget is still being considered at the time of writing.

The Senate also rejected two other crypto-related measures debated as part of the budget.

One was a provision to tax gains realized when holders exchange cryptocurrencies for certain stablecoins.

The second was a proposal to expand France's exit tax to include unrealized gains on cryptocurrencies held by taxpayers who move their tax residence outside the country.

#121769. What Is Pons? The Robinhood Chain Meme Coin Launchpad Explained

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1572 w)

What Is Pons? The Robinhood Chain Meme Coin Launchpad Explained

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1572 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Decrypt

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, when Robinhood switched on its own Robinhood Chain blockchain on July 1, 2026, the trading app's stock tokens were supposed to be the main attraction.
  • Sources indicate that pons became the busiest place to make them.
  • In a recent development, that openness can also be exploited.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, when Robinhood switched on its own Robinhood Chain blockchain on July 1, 2026, the trading app's stock tokens were supposed to be the main attraction. Instead, much of the early activity came from meme coins: tokens built around a joke or an internet trend.

Sources indicate that pons became the busiest place to make them. Like Pump.fun on Solana, it lets anyone pick a name, ticker and image and have a tradable token minutes later, without writing code. Its fees briefly made it one of the highest-earning protocols in crypto, and its own token, PONS, went on to list on Kraken and Coinbase.

In a recent development, that openness can also be exploited. In September 2026, an onchain analyst alleged that one group had used Pons releases to extract millions of dollars from buyers.

This guide explains what Pons is, how its two generations of contracts work, what the PONS token does, and the risks.

Pons is a token launch protocol running on Robinhood Chain, a layer-2 network built on Ethereum using Arbitrum's technology, and its website and documentation are published by Pons Labs, LLC.

In a recent development, every token rolled out through Pons is a standard ERC-20 token with a fixed supply, 1 billion tokens on V1 launches, that can never be increased. The creator gets no allocation set aside before trading opens.

Pons is also non-custodial. Its documentation says every launch and trade is a transaction the user's own wallet signs, and the platform never holds user funds.

In a recent development, pons went live within days of Robinhood Chain's mainnet. It picked up most of the chain's launchpad activity after an early rival, Noxa, stopped accepting newly introduced launches on July 11, 2026, according to Decrypt's reporting.

Pons has two generations of contracts, V1 and V2, and both remain live on Robinhood Chain.

Recent findings suggest that in V1, a single transaction deploys the token and its trading pool, a Uniswap V3 pool paired with wrapped ETH (WETH), and locks the pool's liquidity so the creator can't withdraw it. Each launch costs 0.0005 ETH and carries a 1% trading fee, the documentation indicates. A launch "graduates" once 4.2 ETH has been paired in its pool by default, but trading carries on in the same pool.

Recent findings suggest that V1 debuts are protected for their first two blocks: in the launch block, only the creator's initial buy can execute, and for the rest of the window no wallet can hold more than 5% of supply or buy more than 5.5%. Fees are split 70% to the creator and 30% to the protocol for current launches.

According to recent reports, V2 adds a bonding curve: a contract that holds a token's whole supply and sets its price by formula, rising as people buy and falling as they sell. According to the V2 documentation, the curve sells out, then "graduates" automatically into a Uniswap V4 pool, seeded with a fixed share of supply held back from the start. The pool's liquidity is then locked permanently; no unlock function exists.

V2 debuts can be priced in ETH or in other assets Pons has approved, including tokenized stocks, in which case the creator is paid in that asset. Each trade pays a standard fee shared between Pons, the creator and an optional buyback, plus an optional creator tax that is capped by the protocol and fixed at launch.

In a recent development, when a creator turns buybacks on, part of their own fee is spent buying their token back. Those tokens are locked in a vault and released over five years, split between the creator and the protocol.

PONS itself was launched through Pons's own legacy V1 factory, and its documentation uses PONS as the reference token for developers testing their integrations.

"Sniping" means buying a large share of a new token in its first seconds, often with bots, then selling into later buyers. Every V2 launch opens with a "snipe tax" of 99% on buys that decays to zero over five seconds, the documentation indicates.

The launching wallet and the creator's fee wallet are exempt automatically, and creators can name up to 32 more exempt addresses at launch "for a team bundling its opening buys across several wallets.".

According to recent reports, that exemption became central to allegations published on September 27, 2026. Pseudonymous onchain analyst Wazz tweeted that a single operation had extracted at least $18.43 million from 53 Robinhood Chain releases between July 10 and September 21, 2026, mostly through Pons V2. Wazz stated nearly every launch was sniped for 70% or more of its supply by bundles of 70 to 200 wallets.

I just uncovered the biggest serial Rugpulling and Extraction operation on Robinhood.

The same operation is linked 53 introduces within a 2 month period.

Total Extracted: $18.43 MILLION.

very likely more this is just what I could directly link.

🧵 https://t.co/wS62KAbvv5 pic.twitter.com/BSxZL9wU44.

— Wazz (@WazzCrypto) September 27, 2026.

In a recent development, the Block reviewed the onchain data and found that creators of nine Pons V2 introduces had exempted 15 to 25 wallets each from the snipe tax, which then bought out the bonding curve in a single transaction. The creator and those wallets held 82% to 86% of supply after the opening buys. The Block did not independently replicate Wazz's $18.43 million total.

In a recent development, on September 3, 2026, Pons generated $5.95 million in daily fees, briefly out-earning Robinhood Chain itself and ranking fourth among all protocols tracked by DefiLlama, Decrypt reported. Pons fees drove Robinhood Chain to a record of about $6 million in daily fees in early September 2026, The Block reported.

Sources indicate that on September 5, 2026, blockchain analytics firm Arkham tweeted that crypto market maker Wintermute appeared to be buying PONS slowly in a series of small purchases, and held just over $3 million of the token. Wallets that Arkham attributes to Wintermute held about 3.4 million PONS at the time, and about 7.4 million as of November 2026.

As of November 20, 2026, DefiLlama put Pons's cumulative fees at about $205 million. Of that, $137 million came in September 2026 alone; fees fell to about $17 million in October 2026.

Sources indicate that PONS is the ERC-20 token tied to the Pons launchpad, with a fixed supply of 1 billion. Its link to the platform is a buyback.

According to the V1 documentation, 80% of the protocol's fees are used to buy PONS on the market through an automated process and send it to a burn address, permanently removing it from circulation. The remaining 20% pays for infrastructure and the Pons team. Kraken's listing notice describes the same mechanism.

As of November 20, 2026, CoinGecko data shows about 669 million PONS in circulation, out of a fixed supply of 1 billion.

You can track PONS's latest price on Decrypt's price page.

PONS trades in Uniswap pools on Robinhood Chain. Binance Wallet added it to its Binance Alpha tier on September 2, 2026, and Kraken opened PONS trading on September 25, 2026, with access through the Kraken App and Instant Buy to follow once liquidity allows. Coinbase Markets tweeted on October 6, 2026, that it had added PONS to its listing roadmap, and said the next day that its PONS-USD pair would open later that day, if liquidity conditions were met.

Sources indicate that pons has flagged several changes still to come. Its V1 documentation says the 80% share of protocol fees used to buy back PONS is not yet fixed in its contracts, but will become "immutable, decentralized, and automated" in a future release.

Industry observers note that on V2, three security firms (SB Security, Dingbats and Pashov Audit Group) are reviewing the contracts, and Pons says it will publish their reports in full, including any findings it did not accept, once the reviews close. Until then, its documentation tells users to treat V2 as unaudited, and only whitelisted addresses can create V2 tokens.

Recent findings suggest that pons also faces competition on its home chain. Uniswap, already Robinhood Chain's main exchange, introduced its own launchpad, Pools.trade, on August 5, 2026. It charges no launchpad fee, locks each launch's liquidity permanently, and offers a "crowd launch" option designed to resist bundling. Within its first days, Pools.trade took about half of Robinhood Chain's launchpad volume, Decrypt's Morning Minute newsletter reported. The newsletter noted that Uniswap can afford to forgo launchpad fees because it earns from its other products, which most dedicated launchpads cannot.

Pons has since kept the larger share of fees. As of November 2026, DefiLlama highlighted Pons collecting about $5.6 million in fees over the previous 30 days, against about $115,000 for Pools.trade. The two charge different rates, though: Pools.trade's trading fee is 0.25%, while Pons's standard fee is 1%.

It has been revealed that V2's tokenized-stock pairs link Pons introduces to the stock tokens Robinhood built the chain to carry, which ties Pons's prospects to Robinhood Chain itself. On Robinhood's third-quarter earnings call on October 27, 2026, CEO Vlad Tenev noted the growth of the chain and its ecosystem had exceeded the organization's expectations, and that Robinhood was investing in how to support the chain's developer community.

Home » Blitz news » Fidelity Crypto Adds AAVE, LINK, UNI, Expanding Asset List to Eight.

Fidelity Investments adds three DeFi tokens to its retail lineup.

In a recent development, fidelity Investments has added AAVE, Chainlink (LINK) and Uniswap (UNI) to its Fidelity Crypto trading service, expanding its supported digital asset list from five to eight. The addition lifts the number of supported assets from five to eight and brings three DeFi tokens to eligible US customers.

Recent findings suggest that fidelity unveiled the update on its official website and in an X post. The platform now supports Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), Solana (SOL), Litecoin (LTC), AAVE, LINK, UNI and the Fidelity Digital Dollar (FIDD), a US dollar-pegged stablecoin the tech giant announced in January 2026.

Sources indicate that each upcoming token is tied to a different part of DeFi. AAVE is the token for Aave, a lending protocol that mediates cryptocurrency lending and borrowing.

Industry observers note that UNI is the governance token for Uniswap, a decentralized exchange. LINK is used in Chainlink, an oracle network that delivers external information such as price data to smart contracts.

It has been revealed that trading and custody are handled by Fidelity Digital Assets, a subsidiary licensed as a U.S. National Trust Bank. The service is available to eligible U.S. customers aged 18 and over residing in states where Fidelity provides the service.

Fidelity launched Fidelity Crypto for individual investors in 2022, initially offering Bitcoin and Ether. The latest addition follows Charles Schwab’s November 9 listing of Solana, Avalanche and Chainlink on its spot crypto platform.

Fidelity’s addition of AAVE, UNI and LINK extends a major US brokerage’s retail crypto offering to DeFi infrastructure tokens. It also adds to competition among traditional brokerages for crypto-active customers, following Schwab’s recent expansion.

SpaceX could announce $1.5 trillion Tesla merger in December: report

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1023 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that elon Musk’s companies are moving faster than expected on a Tesla-SpaceX combination.
  • Tesla holds its annual shareholder meeting on December 3, and the same directors who would sign off on the deal are up for re-election.
  • According to Bloomberg’s sources, it’s now a negotiation over price and control, with boards and advisers on both sides involved.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that elon Musk’s companies are moving faster than expected on a Tesla-SpaceX combination. A deal could be announced as soon as December, which would make it the largest merger ever, according to Bloomberg.

Tesla holds its annual shareholder meeting on December 3, and the same directors who would sign off on the deal are up for re-election.

According to Bloomberg’s sources, it’s now a negotiation over price and control, with boards and advisers on both sides involved. December is the target, but early 2027 is also on the table.

In a recent development, one of the variables on the table is how many SpaceX shares Tesla investors would receive. So, as expected, this is shaping up as SpaceX absorbing Tesla, not the other way around.

Recent findings suggest that that fits the valuations. SpaceX is worth over $1.9 trillion after its June IPO, while Tesla sits around $1.5 trillion. For scale, the record for a single deal has long been Vodafone’s $183 billion takeover of Mannesmann in 2000, and even SpaceX’s roughly $250 billion purchase of xAI (a private manufacturer at the time) earlier this year would be dwarfed.

According to recent reports, neither company commented. Tesla stock rose as much as 1.9% on the report.

We’ve been tracking this since May, when Musk first floated merging the two companies weeks before the SpaceX IPO. At the time, we called it the fourth time Musk would make a more than $1 billion self-dealing transaction, after SolarCity, Twitter/X, and Tesla’s $2 billion xAI investment that turned into SpaceX stock.

It has been revealed that then, in October, Tesla’s proxy filing read like a board getting ready for a SpaceX merger. Ira Ehrenpreis, who chairs Tesla’s compensation and governance committees, has sat on SpaceX’s board since February. The ballot for the December 3 meeting is limited to re-electing Musk, chair Robyn Denholm, and JB Straubel to terms through 2029, plus a say-on-pay vote and the auditor.

A day later, Musk confirmed that both boards had formed special committees to explore a merger.

The governance piece is where Tesla shareholders should pay the most attention.

Industry observers note that musk owns about 20% of Tesla but controlled roughly 85% of SpaceX’s voting power through super-voting shares, according to its S-1. Swapping Tesla shares for SpaceX shares means trading one-share-one-vote for a tech giant where Musk’s control is effectively locked in.

Sources indicate that and the deal itself pays Musk. Under the change-in-control terms in his 2025 CEO award, the operational milestones drop out and the market cap test runs at the deal price, with earned shares vesting immediately. Based on the share count in the proxy, a deal valuing Tesla at $2 trillion (about a 33% premium to where it trades now) would clear the first market cap tranche on the spot. His 286 million restricted shares from the 2018 package also accelerate on a change in control.

In a recent development, bloomberg reports that one of the main obstacles is how to ring-fence Tesla’s China business. A JPMorgan analyst described SpaceX’s defense and government work and Tesla’s China footprint as “key dynamics that are at odds with each other” for regulators and shareholders.

That’s the same problem behind the Wall Street Journal’s July report that Tesla was weighing a sale or spinoff of its China operations, which Musk denied. Giga Shanghai is Tesla’s most productive factory and builds more than half of its cars. It shipped 67,829 vehicles in October alone.

Politics is the other wild card. Congress flipped to Democrats in the midterms, and they’ve stated Musk’s companies and his political ties will get a hard look. Bloomberg previously reported the companies want to close before President Trump leaves office.

Sources indicate that I suspected that the midterms might accelerate the timeline. The Dems don’t take office until January, and Musk likely wants to move this as far along as possible before then.

No rational independent board would offer $1.5 trillion (much less $2 trillion) for Tesla. It is a shrinking EV manufacturer with a few fantasy projects that are not delivering. But endlessly diluting other stockholders is his thing.

According to recent reports, as for the “independent committees”, those are obviously a joke. No one believes that, but it’s not like Tesla’s shareholders would care at this point. Tesla’s stock has been a dud for 4 years, and shareholders’ best chance to see a return is another self-deal with Musk.

Tesla is a car and energy organization with falling car sales, and it would get folded into a rocket, satellite, and AI company that’s valued at a premium to it and controlled by one person.

Sources indicate that this is the end game. At least, it looks like Elon is running out of companies to fold together to hide underperformance.

Industry observers note that if you’re following Tesla because of its energy business, the cheapest way to tap into that transition at home is still putting solar on your own roof. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs.
