Shiba Inu (SHIB) kept leaving crypto exchanges this week as the price of the meme cryptocurrency fell to levels last seen in the spring of 2021, and on Wednesday, the outflow picked up sharply.

Sources indicate that according to CoinGlass data, 520.83 billion SHIB left exchanges over the past 24 hours. That amount made up most of the 757.51 billion SHIB that exchanges lost over the past seven days, and over the past 30 days, the outflow reached 2.88 trillion SHIB.

Recent findings suggest that on Wednesday evening, SHIB was trading at $0.00000344, according to CoinGlass. So far this week, the token was down 4.78%, and its market capitalization went down to $2.02 billion, according to TradingView.

Sources indicate that according to the weekly chart on TradingView, SHIB last traded at these levels in the spring of 2021, months before the token reached its all-time high of $0.00008845 on Oct. 28, 2021.

Recent findings suggest that from early 2026 until mid-November, the price of SHIB held above $0.000004, and the yearly low stood at $0.00000411 at the July 17 close. In November, SHIB fell to $0.00000373, and in late November, the token dropped as low as $0.00000337. On Jan. 1, the token closed the day at $0.00000692, and since the start of the year, SHIB has lost 50.3% of its value, according to CoinGlass. As of Nov. 22, SHIB had lost 22.7% in November so far, according to CryptoRank.

The latest drop in SHIB came after Bitcoin fell back below $60,000 this week. On Saturday, Nov. 21, Bitcoin dropped as low as $55,150, its lowest price since September 2024. Over the past 24 hours, $57,590 worth of SHIB futures positions were liquidated, and $54,750 of that amount came from long positions on OKX, according to CoinGlass.

Industry observers note that the Wednesday outflow was not the first large one this month. On Nov. 17, about 312 billion SHIB were withdrawn from exchanges, according to CryptoQuant. On the same day, the number of SHIB holders on Ethereum passed 1.7 million, according to Etherscan.

It has been revealed that coinGlass data also demonstrates that since late 2024, the total SHIB balance on exchanges has gone down by 19.18 trillion tokens, or 20.54%, to 74.19 trillion, and over the same period, the price of SHIB fell by 88.39%. The remaining 74.19 trillion SHIB on exchanges make up 12.59% of the circulating supply and are worth about $254.75 million.

Industry observers note that most of the 24-hour outflow came from exchanges that CoinGlass groups as "Others," as their combined SHIB balance fell by 88.5% to 70.93 billion tokens. Over the same period, the SHIB balances of Binance and OKX barely changed, and Coinbase, Bitfinex and Bitstamp added SHIB.

As a result, in the week when the price of SHIB fell to levels last seen in 2021, exchanges lost more SHIB in a single day than over the previous six days combined, according to CoinGlass data.

UK to test whether AI can replace a second mammogram reader in trial of 660,000 women

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Women in Cambridgeshire are the first to join a UK trial testing whether AI can take on the second check of a screening mammogram.
  • The study will compare two AI approaches with the usual two-reader process, and researchers will measure how many cancers each approach detects and how often women are called back for further tests.
  • NIHR Cambridge reported the first enrollments on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women in Cambridgeshire are the first to join a UK trial testing whether AI can take on the second check of a screening mammogram.

The study will compare two AI approaches with the usual two-reader process, and researchers will measure how many cancers each approach detects and how often women are called back for further tests.

NIHR Cambridge reported the first enrollments on Nov. 23. The study, known as EDITH, aims to enroll 660,000 women across about 30 UK breast screening centers, according to the ISRCTN trial registry.

Eligible women receive information about the trial and how to opt out with their screening invitation. The appointment itself proceeds as usual, and every mammogram in the trial still gets at least one human read.

EDITH randomly assigns clinic days to one of three approaches, and each participating center uses all three. Under standard screening, two NHS experts read the images. In one trial arm, an expert reads the mammogram first, then AI checks for signs of cancer the expert may have missed.

In the other AI arm, the software assesses the images first, and one NHS expert reads mammograms the tool rates as low likelihood for cancer, and two read those it rates as high likelihood.

Recent findings suggest that A very high score or a disagreement about whether to call a woman back sends the case for an additional human review. Across all three groups, at least two human experts make final decisions about cancer detection.

It has been revealed that the trial compares two AI workflows with standard double reading. In the AI-first workflow, the tool scores how likely the images are to show cancer.

Every mammogram gets at least one human read. At least two human experts make final decisions about cancer detection.

The diagram shows the trial’s assigned reading steps. Researchers will use cancer detection and callback rates to compare the approaches.

The three lanes map the assigned screening pathways in the registered EDITH study design. The branch in the triage arm shows how AI-assessed likelihood determines the number of initial human reads.

In a recent development, the diagram reveals the trial’s assigned reading steps. Researchers will use cancer detection and callback rates to compare the approaches.

Researchers will compare each AI approach separately with standard double reading.

The registered study design treats at least one additional cancer detected per 1,000 women screened as a meaningful gain. For recalls, it sets a comparison margin of up to two extra callbacks per 1,000 women screened relative to standard double reading.

Both rates are calculated across all women screened.

Recent findings suggest that the two rates capture different steps in screening, and staff counts a callback when they ask a woman to return for more tests. The cancer detection rate counts cancers found during the screening episode.

Sources indicate that researchers will count how many readings staff carry out, how many cases need an extra expert review, and how many women are called back for assessment. The study will also track cancers found between screening rounds.

NIHR Cambridge says the NHS would change routine screening only if the evidence demonstrates the latest approach is as safe and effective as the care women receive today.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lunar Energy has unveiled a 25-kW home DC fast charger that will do more than just power up your car really fast.
  • The new battery system will be available to customers in early 2027, with the charger rollout expected in mid-2027.
  • In a recent development, lunar claims its home DC fast charger can add roughly 100 miles of range in an hour at up to 25 kW.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lunar Energy has unveiled a 25-kW home DC fast charger that will do more than just power up your car really fast. Paired with its next-generation home battery system, the Lunar Fast Charger will also let a compatible EV help keep the house running during an outage and potentially earn money by sending electricity back to the grid.

The new battery system will be available to customers in early 2027, with the charger rollout expected in mid-2027.

In a recent development, lunar claims its home DC fast charger can add roughly 100 miles of range in an hour at up to 25 kW. Actual results will depend on the vehicle and charging conditions.

This is a DC charger, according to Lunar’s product specifications. It connects directly to the DC side of the Lunar Battery, and Lunar says that setup avoids an electrical panel upgrade for the charger. The product page lists CCS and NACS connector support but doesn’t specify which cars will support bidirectional charging.

Recent findings suggest that that distinction matters. Charging an EV and sending power back are separate capabilities, so buyers will need to check vehicle compatibility before relying on home backup.

In a recent development, with a compatible EV, Lunar states vehicle-to-home (V2H) charging could extend backup power through a multi-day outage. How long it lasts will depend on the car’s available battery capacity and what’s running in the house.

Industry observers note that vehicle-to-grid (V2G) payments will also depend on the availability of programs. They aren’t an automatic benefit of installing the charger.

The updated Lunar System has a 13.4 kW inverter and uses 5 kWh battery modules. A single tower holds 10–30 kWh, while towers installed side by side can provide up to 300 kWh.

Lunar is also expanding into small businesses, with pad-mounted configurations reaching 1 MWh. Businesses could use the batteries for backup and to reduce demand charges, or fees tied to their highest power draw.

In a recent development, the system can work with fresh solar using Lunar Maximizer panel optimizers, existing solar, or no solar at all. Lunar says assembly takes place in California, Georgia, Idaho, and Washington, with engineering and R&D in Mountain View, California.

Lunar AI uses electricity prices, weather forecasts, and a property’s energy use to decide when to charge batteries or supply power. Adding the EV gives it another battery to coordinate with rooftop solar and household battery storage.

The company reports that its California customers using Lunar AI saved an additional $338 on average last year compared with a standard battery operating mode.

It has been revealed that lunar’s Gridshare platform already manages more than 150,000 distributed energy devices worldwide. It groups those resources into virtual power plants (VPPs), allowing utilities and other energy providers to call on stored electricity when demand rises and offer customers incentives for participating. It presently operates VPPs in California, Hawaii, and Texas and is expanding in Utah, Nevada, and Fresh Jersey. It also operates in Europe, the UK, and Japan.

Sources indicate that lunar hasn’t yet disclosed pricing or named compatible bidirectional EV models. Those are two crucial details homeowners will need before deciding whether this setup makes sense for their driveway.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Upcoming capital gains tax reforms are prompting crypto holders to reconsider how they access cash without selling their digital assets.
  • One in five Australian cryptocurrency investors would consider borrowing against their digital assets rather than selling them, as upcoming tax changes push holders to rethink their financial strategies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Crypto Market News » Australian Crypto Investors Turn to Loans Ahead of 2027 Tax Reform.

Upcoming capital gains tax reforms are prompting crypto holders to reconsider how they access cash without selling their digital assets.

One in five Australian cryptocurrency investors would consider borrowing against their digital assets rather than selling them, as upcoming tax changes push holders to rethink their financial strategies.

A survey commissioned by digital asset wealth platform Nexo found that 22.7% of Australian crypto holders would consider borrowing against their holdings instead of selling, compared with 10% of other investors.

The findings come as Australia prepares to overhaul its capital gains tax (CGT) system from July 1, 2027.

Nexo surveyed 1,000 Australian investors this October to examine how major expenses and rising living costs affect investment decisions.

The results suggest that crypto holders are more inclined to avoid selling their investments when they need additional funds.

Beyond the 22.7% considering borrowing, another 19.7% mentioned they had delayed or decided against selling their crypto holdings.

Industry observers note that crypto investors can borrow against their existing holdings instead of selling them for cash. This allows them to access money while keeping their Bitcoin or other digital assets, and potentially benefit if their value increases.

The trend comes against a broader backdrop of financial pressure. According to the survey, 29.4% of all investors had delayed, reduced or cancelled a major purchase or financial strategy over the previous 12 months.

The upcoming CGT reform is another factor investors may need to consider.

Under Australia’s current system, eligible individuals, trusts and partnerships can receive a 50% capital gains tax discount on assets held for more than 12 months.

From July 1, 2027, this discount will be replaced by cost base indexation and a 30% minimum tax on eligible gains.

Under transitional arrangements, gains accrued before that date will remain eligible for the existing 50% discount, while gains accumulated afterward will be subject to the new rules.

Crypto ownership in Australia is at a record high, with 2.79 million Australians holding or trading cryptocurrency, according to the figures cited in an Australian investor Study.

That equals about 24% of the country’s 11.5 million investors, up from roughly 15% in 2023, making crypto as widely held as exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

As ownership expands, the demand for financial products that allow investors to access liquidity without selling their holdings could also increase.

Consequently, as their holdings rise in value, more investors may look for ways to cover major expenses without selling their crypto.

Industry observers note that the newly introduced CGT rules could make some investors think twice before selling crypto that has increased in value. As a result, more holders may consider borrowing against their holdings to cover major expenses without having to sell their assets and potentially trigger a capital gains tax bill.

Recent findings suggest that the Franklin Crypto Index ETF is preparing to add Hyperliquid to its portfolio, according to a prospectus supplement filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Wednesday.

The fund currently holds Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Dogecoin, Solana, Cardano and Stellar.

In a recent development, the HYPE token will be held in spot, with its allocation determined by its weighting in the underlying CF Benchmarks index. The fund is expected to maintain a portfolio structure broadly aligned with the index.

Recent findings suggest that the move comes as major trader Abraxas Capital reportedly exited its Hyperliquid position on Wednesday. The firm is stated to have generated approximately $530 million in profits from the trade.

In September, Hashdex added HYPE to its Nasdaq CME Crypto Index ETF, with a 3.36% weighting.

Currently, there are three Hyperliquid ETFs: THYP and HYPG by 21Shares, and Bitwise's BHYP. Their combined assets, however, remain relatively low, currently under $259 million.

Hyperliquid is trading near $59.8, down 1.3% over the past 24 hours and 10.2% over the previous week.

In a recent development, the $55-$56 range is an immediate support area. A move above $60 could signal declining selling pressure, while a decline below the range could lead to more liquidations and further correction.

HYPE has slipped below its major moving averages, including the 200-day moving average near $68, reinforcing the bearish outlook.

Meanwhile, the RSI hovers around 35, indicating weakening momentum and approaching oversold conditions.

Sources indicate that the market is also preparing for an important token unlock scheduled for Dec. 6. Reports estimate that the release could be worth $578 million at current prices.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andrew Webley, CEO of The Smarter Web Manufacturer, stated that Bitcoin's drop has been sharper than he had anticipated, but he does not think the digital asset's price will decline much further.

The British CEO, whose firm recently added 55 BTC to its treasury, said investors' opinions on Bitcoin can shift considerably without any changes to Bitcoin itself.

Industry observers note that "Sentiment towards Bitcoin can change very quickly. Without Bitcoin changing at all," Webley mentioned on X.

It has been revealed that webley advised investors to consider Bitcoin's movements relative to other assets. Bitcoin's price decline indicates investors how much the cryptocurrency has lost in absolute terms.

However, Bitcoin's performance relative to the broader market may indicate BTC is being sold specifically or whether investors are taking profits across multiple markets. Webley did not specify which assets he was comparing Bitcoin against.

"Do I expect Bitcoin to go significantly lower from here? No. But as the past few weeks have shown, predicting short-term price movements is a very challenging task," Webley noted.

Some of the most challenging periods for investors, he said, were followed by some of his most profitable periods.

His most definitive prediction concerned Bitcoin's longer-term outlook: "Bitcoin has an incredible future.".

In fact, Webley's firm has been buying more Bitcoin as its price has been dropping.

On Nov. 17, Smarter Web stated it spent around £2.75 million on 55 BTC, bringing its total holdings to 2,905 BTC.

The average purchase price was £49,991 per Bitcoin, roughly 38% below the treasury's overall average purchase price of £81,234 following the transaction.

Recent findings suggest that smarter Web borrowed around £2.6 million under its Coinbase credit facility to finance most of the purchase. The firm used its existing Bitcoin holdings as collateral.

Following the transaction, Smarter Web had around £19 million outstanding under the dollar-denominated credit facility.

BYD wins round one in Defender-copycat battle as JLR is told to destroy documents

💡 Key Takeaways
  • BYD just got some good news in its Defender-copycat court battle with JLR.
  • After BYD opened orders for the Ti 7 in Europe and the UK in late July, many (including us at Electrek) compared it to the iconic Land Rover Defender, with its boxy, rugged (yet still elegant) SUV design.
  • BYD even described it as having “an unapologetically boxy profile” that delivers “the imposing, chunky design that finds favour among SUV buyers, yet delivers a contemporary look.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD just got some good news in its Defender-copycat court battle with JLR. After JLR had BYD’s Netherlands offices raided and documents seized, a Dutch court has now handed BYD an early win, ordering JLR to destroy the documents or face a penalty.

After BYD opened orders for the Ti 7 in Europe and the UK in late July, many (including us at Electrek) compared it to the iconic Land Rover Defender, with its boxy, rugged (yet still elegant) SUV design.

BYD even described it as having “an unapologetically boxy profile” that delivers “the imposing, chunky design that finds favour among SUV buyers, yet delivers a contemporary look.”.

In August, authorities on behalf of the British luxury automaker raided BYD’s offices in the Netherlands without prior warning and seized digital records.

On November 11, a Dutch court in The Hague ruled against JLR and ordered the company to destroy the seized documents, which included launch aims and other technical data, so they wouldn’t fall into anyone else’s hands.

JLR must destroy the documents within 24 hours of the ruling or face a fine of €50,000 ($55,000) for every hour it is delayed, with a maximum penalty of up to €500,000 ($553,000).

Within 24 hours of destroying it, JLR must also provide BYD with third-party confirmation that it has been destroyed. The court also rejected the British automaker’s request to pay a €500,000 ($553,000) fine.

According to Autoweek Netherlands, the ruling is based on the fact that JLR doesn’t need the documents, noting that the Ti 7 has not yet been sold in the European Union.

BYD won the ruling, and JLR is prohibited from taking any further legal action under the initial seizure order, but JLR has already begun summary proceedings over the infringement in Rotterdam and The Hague.

JLR claims that the Ti 7 SUV is a “slavish imitation” and infringes on the intellectual property of the Land Rover Defender and that BYD stripped down the Defender to reverse-engineer some of its technology.

Before the raid, BYD claims it fully cooperated with JLR’s requests. BYD’s lawyers called the British automakers’ raid a “fishing expedition” and claimed that “too many files were seized.”.

Sources indicate that the Ti 7 is on sale starting at £47,995 ($64,000) in the UK, on the road. That’s over £20,000 ($26,500) less than the plug-in Defender 110, which starts at £71,840 ($95,500) in the UK.

It has a seven-seat arrangement, which BYD said was specifically designed for the European and UK markets.

As the first vehicle in the UK based on its DM-p (Dual Mode performance) powertrain, BYD said the Ti 7 “vastly exceeds the closest competition,” seemingly another jab at the Defender.

"JLR believes BYD stripped down the Defender to reverse engineer some of its technology".

Reverse engineering isn't illegal. Patent infringement is illegal.

Competition strip down each other's product all the time. As long as they don't use the "exact" same technology, it isn't a copy right issue.

The setup uses three electric motors and a 1.5-liter turbocharged engine, delivering a combined 402 hp (408 PS), enabling it to accelerate from 0 to 62 mph in 4.8 seconds.

It has been revealed that the engine primarily powers a 35.6 kWh BYD Blade Battery, which provides a pure-electric WLTP driving range of up to 74 miles. In the city, it has an electric range of up to 102 miles.

Available exclusively in the UK in the flagship Excellence AWD trim, BYD claims that the Ti 7 offers “a level of equipment that exceeds anything that its rivals can offer at this price point.”.

We should learn more about the BYD and JLR legal battle soon. Check back for updates, as this story is still ongoing.

Industry observers note that the sentiment is bitter & the market mood resembles that of November 2022, latest research from Bitrue’s Research Institute states. The analysts at Bitrue analyzed a multi-cycle market data bundle from 2022 to 2026, showcasing similar levels of ‘extreme fear’ around 20.

Schmidt’s chart examines XRP’s weekly price from 2017 through 2026, highlighting nearly-identical patterns across several market cycles.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • That's Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong's take on Bitcoin investor behavior, less than a week after the record-breaking $93.5 billion IPO of Claude creator Anthropic.
  • "Historically, people rotate out of it to take advantage of a big IPO.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that "Bitcoin investors tend to sell BTC when there's a big IPO. Then they come back.".

That's Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong's take on Bitcoin investor behavior, less than a week after the record-breaking $93.5 billion IPO of Claude creator Anthropic.

"Historically, people rotate out of it to take advantage of a big IPO. Then they come back in," Armstrong wrote on X earlier today.

Industry observers note that the limited window of opportunity to invest in an IPO helps explain the behavior Armstrong described. For an investor to buy at the IPO price, there's only a certain period during which they can request an allocation of shares. After that, the price is determined by the market.

On Nov. 19, Anthropic went public on the Nasdaq, and that brief window of opportunity mattered.

It has been revealed that shares were priced at $83, up from the $70-$78 range indicated just two days earlier. Anthropic's stock, trading under the ticker ANT, opened at $111.50.

If you bought at that opening price, you paid about 34% more per share than an investor who received an allocation at the IPO price.

Recent findings suggest that when the IPO closed on Nov. 20, 1.127 billion shares had been sold, including 147 million additional shares purchased by underwriters exercising their option.

Industry observers note that of the $93.5 billion in gross proceeds, Anthropic itself received around $91.6 billion. The rest went to existing shareholders.

There was also a separate $26 billion private placement involving investors such as Microsoft, Nvidia, Google and others. In total, the combined transactions were valued at $119.5 billion.

As for the longer-term case for holding BTC, Armstrong's point concerns investors' expectations about the future purchasing power of their money.

"If you think there is going to be more inflation and money printing in the future, bitcoin is as important as ever.".

At the heart of the matter is Bitcoin's 21 million supply limit.

If you expect governments to continue expanding the money supply, you may still be excited by the prospect of a major IPO. And you may sell some of your BTC to participate in it.

Armstrong's argument is that the window of opportunity to participate in a major IPO eventually closes.

However, the reasons investors bought Bitcoin in the first place may remain long after the newly listed stock starts trading.

sonnen’s newly introduced smart breakers help your home battery last longer

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A home battery can do more during a blackout if it isn’t busy running nonessential, energy-hungry appliances.
  • The companies confirmed today that they’re integrating ADAPT Energy’s controls and Eaton AbleEdge smart breakers into the SOLRITE–sonnen virtual power plant (VPP).
  • The announcement doesn’t specify pricing, how many homes will receive it, or when existing customers can get it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A home battery can do more during a blackout if it isn’t busy running nonessential, energy-hungry appliances. sonnen and SOLRITE Energy are putting that same principle to work for the grid, adding smart breakers that can temporarily switch off selected household loads while batteries help meet electricity demand.

The companies confirmed today that they’re integrating ADAPT Energy’s controls and Eaton AbleEdge smart breakers into the SOLRITE–sonnen virtual power plant (VPP). The setup combines sonnenHub with breakers that manage power-hungry equipment, both during outages and when the grid needs help.

The announcement doesn’t specify pricing, how many homes will receive it, or when existing customers can get it.

A VPP connects home batteries into a network so they can work together as a larger energy resource. This addition gives SOLRITE another way to respond: in addition to controlling the batteries, it can reduce the amount of electricity that participating homes use.

Recent findings suggest that sonnen and SOLRITE used the example of a pool pump, as it’s energy-intensive, nonessential, and runs for longer periods. When an event begins, ADAPT temporarily switches off the pool pump while the sonnen battery sends electricity to the grid.

Sources indicate that with less battery power going toward the pump, more can flow to the grid. Across participating homes, that gives the VPP more flexibility than relying on battery dispatch alone.

It has been revealed that homeowners have to opt in to that grid participation, and ADAPT will switch off only pre-approved household loads. Joining the VPP program doesn’t give the operator blanket permission to turn off anything in the house.

“Instead of putting the pressure on homeowners to change the way their home is wired, and to manually manipulate loads during an outage, we’re putting intelligence into their energy system, which provides a seamless and automatic backup power experience for their home,” mentioned Troy Morgan, president of PanTech Design, the developer of ADAPT Energy.

The breakers also tackle a practical problem with home backup: Massive appliances can drain a battery promptly, and the surge of power some equipment needs to start can overload a backup system just as an outage begins.

Industry observers note that ADAPT coordinates the smart breakers with the sonnen battery to automatically switch off large loads during backup operation. When grid power returns, it restores them, so homeowners don’t have to go around resetting individual circuits.

Sources indicate that that also gives homeowners more flexibility later. According to the companies, changing which smart-breaker-controlled loads are switched off during an outage doesn’t require rewiring those circuits.

Sources indicate that the installation benefit matters, too. Some backup setups require electricians to move selected circuits into a separate panel. This system manages compatible circuits where their breakers already sit, which the companies say reduces installation complexity and inspection work.

According to recent reports, whole-home backup still has limits. Automatically managing large loads helps the available battery capacity go further; it doesn’t mean every appliance can run at once throughout an outage.

Sources indicate that SOLRITE finances, builds, and owns residential solar-plus-storage projects through what it calls Virtual Power Plant Agreements, with no upfront cost to homeowners. It claims it operates in Texas, California, Connecticut, Massachusetts, and Illinois, with more markets planned.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • On the same date, BlockchainCenter’s dynamic version displayed “BUY!”.
  • The two readings describe the same selloff from different starting points.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that on BlockchainCenter's original Bitcoin Rainbow Chart, the price marker sat below the bottom purple band, and the chart labeled the reading “Bitcoin is dead,” as Bitcoin traded below $59,000 on Nov. 25.

On the same date, BlockchainCenter’s dynamic version displayed “BUY!”.

The two readings describe the same selloff from different starting points. BlockchainCenter presents the original and dynamic charts separately, and each version measures Bitcoin against its own curve.

The original chart snapshot uses a fixed formula dating to 2014, while the dynamic chart fits its curve to daily Bitcoin prices starting in 2012.

It has been revealed that the colored bands show where the price sits relative to each model’s estimate of its long-term trend. As the original curve rises over time, it takes a higher dollar price to reach the same band.

The dynamic model’s estimate can also change as new price history comes in, and the apparent instructions in the labels take their meaning from the curve each chart uses.

BlockchainCenter puts Bitcoin’s price against two different trends.

A price below the bands on the original chart can coexist with a buy label on the dynamic chart.

Publisher readings for November 25, 2026.

Schematic bands compare BlockchainCenter’s two published readings for November 25, 2026. The displayed dollar value belongs to the original chart snapshot.

Publisher readings for November 25, 2026.

BlockchainCenter’s weekly archive demonstrates that the same “Bitcoin is dead” label was recorded for $74,382 on Nov. 8, $65,118 on Nov. 15, and $60,944 on Nov. 22.

Recent findings suggest that the Nov. 25 digest also showed it, with Bitcoin below $59,000, and the label had already appeared at weekly checkpoints in May and October.

According to recent reports, the November readings capture prices on specific dates, so they leave room for swings in between. Bitcoin can keep falling after the original chart runs out of colors, since the quoted prices capture changes the label obscures once the old chart reaches its lower limit.

In March 2020, Bitcoin briefly slipped below the chart’s lowest band during the pandemic crash, according to BlockchainCenter’s history.

Sources indicate that it broke the old boundary again in 2022 when the price fell below $20,000. After the second break, BlockchainCenter added a band beneath its previous floor. The original formula stayed in place, and the new indigo band was labeled “1BTC = 1BTC.”.

BlockchainCenter’s creator states the added band also came under pressure, so the site revised the formula in a separate V2 release on Nov. 21, 2022, using more price history to fit a new curve.

Adding a band changed how the old chart displayed low prices, and refitting the curve changed the benchmark itself. Either change could put a price that had fallen outside the old bands on the chart, even before a recovery.

The fourth Bitcoin halving in April 2024 cut the block subsidy to 3.125 BTC, offering a starting point for comparing the rally that followed with the original curve.

Bitcoin went on to set a dollar record, reaching about $126,200 on Oct. 6, 2025. Even that rally stayed short of the yellow and red bands in the portion of the original chart shown in the Nov. 25 snapshot.

In a recent development, bitcoin recovered from the March 2020 shock and went on to trade well above its 2022 lows. Those recoveries show how different the market can look after a break.

In November, the original chart’s label stayed in place as the price fell, while the dynamic chart put it in a band labeled “BUY!” BlockchainCenter describes the Rainbow Chart as a way to view long-term price history.

The chart’s creator presents even the updated fit as a way to put past price moves in context.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Regulations » Ukraine Legalizes Crypto After One-Day Delay.

Crypto-embracing Bill No. 10225-d gets the highest-priority treatment following a slight procedural delay.

Ukraine’s parliament has approved a bill to bring cryptocurrency trading, custody and taxation under a formal legal framework.

The measure, Bill No. 10225-d, passed after lawmakers postponed consideration a day earlier, a pause that had raised questions about its immediate path despite renewed support from the parliamentary finance committee for the revised text.

The Ukraine crypto bill is designed to legalize and regulate the domestic virtual-asset market rather than leave it in a largely undefined legal space.

Its scope includes tax treatment for crypto activity as well as rules for trading platforms and custodial services.

That approach would place businesses handling customer assets under a clearer licensing and compliance structure.

In a recent development, BREAKING: Ukraine officially passes law to LEGALIZE crypto, effective July 1, 2027. pic.twitter.com/6KxnNa7N2b.

The framework comes into practice on July 1, 2027. It offers more certainty over how digital-asset transactions are treated by authorities, though implementation details will matter as much as the legislation itself.

Ukraine has maintained an active crypto sector despite the strains of war, with digital assets playing a visible role in fundraising and cross-border transfers.

Formalizing the market has therefore carried significance beyond ordinary financial regulation: it could help define how crypto businesses operate in an economy still managing exceptional pressures with the fifth year of war with Russia coming along.

The Ukraine crypto bill’s journey highlights how rapidly crypto policy can shift even when lawmakers broadly support regulation.

BREAKING: Zelensky President of Ukraine officially legalizes Bitcoin & crypto after parliament passes the bill with 271 vote pic.twitter.com/qt9C7jcNVK.

The November 24, 2026 postponement followed committee backing for a revised version, while the subsequent passage points to a resolution of at least some of those immediate obstacles.

Questions remain over the final tax mechanics, the timing of licensing requirements and which agencies will oversee different parts of the sector. Market participants will also watch for secondary rules that determine the practical burden on exchanges, brokers and wallet providers.

Ukraine’s crypto move matters because it adds another sizable European market pursuing rules for digital assets rather than relying on prohibition or legal ambiguity.

The Ukraine crypto legislation may give local firms a route toward greater legitimacy, but the ultimate test will be whether the resulting framework is workable enough to retain innovation while improving crypto oversight.

Review: Engwe’s M20 3.0 is a 60V Super73 killer at a fraction of the price

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (948 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Engwe has impressed us repeatedly with its value e-bikes at lower-than-believable prices.
  • The Engwe M20 3.0 is a specs monster and blows away the original version of the bike released in 2023:.
  • According to recent reports, the M20 is fairly easy to assemble.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Engwe has impressed us repeatedly with its value e-bikes at lower-than-believable prices. But lately, the brand is climbing the value chain with impressive e-bikes that aren’t just great value but also pack strong specs and impressive features. The Engwe M20 3.0 is a great example….

The Engwe M20 3.0 is a specs monster and blows away the original version of the bike released in 2023:.

According to recent reports, the M20 is fairly easy to assemble. At just over 100lbs, it is a bit hard to move around, but once assembled, it feels like a pretty impressive piece of machinery. I love the street tires on here instead of pretending to be an off-roader. Dual bright headlights and brake light with turn signals really give this thing some street cred. Adding to the safety roster, Engwe upgraded the quad-piston brakes with sporty red calipers and 202 mm rotors. This is not a value bike. The rear suspension is tight, which is great for 2 riders but might feel stiff out of the box for light riders. The seat is *chef’s kiss* even for 2 riders. Very soft and comfortable but not too soft. It even has a little ‘gas tank’ storage area aft the seat, which is keyed and enough to hold a few sandwiches, some riding gloves, or a small purse.

It has been revealed that one gripe: There are 3 sets of keys on here, the aforementioned storage area and one set each for each battery. We’d love to see these things keyed together.

The bike/moped/moto came with a huge 1.2 kW battery (or 2 in our case – unless you have a 80-mile commute, 1 should be plenty) that must be charged individually. But with a 60V 8A charger, each one only takes about 2-3 hours to charge, which is impressive.

According to recent reports, I did not expect to like the ride of this thing as much as I did. We can dispense with the pleasantries here; it came set to Class 2 mode with a 20mph top speed and stickers to match; a quick Google search will show you how to open this up to 40mph open mode. I take responsibility for my own actions.

The first thing you’ll notice here is that the motor is whisper-quiet, and with the street tires, there is very little road noise, even at 35mph. The half throttle is plenty responsive, a lot more so than the cadence sensor on the pedals, which are vestigial at best here. Those significant brakes are a bit softer than I’d prefer, but given a good squeeze, those 203mm rotors and quad-piston hydraulic brakes are going to stop you, the 100lb bike, and your passenger/cargo fairly swiftly.

My girlfriend and I got pulled over for the first time in my e-biking life as I was picking her up at the coffee shop. The cop was immediately apologetic because “he thought we were kids” and not the 50-year-olds under the helmets he encountered. Then he noticed the pedals and said that we’re all clear and that what we were on looked like a motorcycle and that a couple of e-moto kids had gotten into accidents recently, one hit by a drunk driver and who is still in a coma. While he was already letting us go, I pointed out the Class 2 sticker on the bike, and he gave me the thumbs-up as we sped off at 30mph. This M20 passed the local police test with flying colors. I can’t guarantee you’ll have the same experience in your jurisdiction.

Industry observers note that most of my gripes on this e-bike are inherent to the form factor. It is heavy at over 100 lbs, but you’d expect that with a 3.3kW motor, 2.4kW of batteries, and room for two. That remarked, don’t buy this bike if you need to take it up stairs or proposal to pedal it without assist. In fact, this isn’t a bikepath bike or a put it on the back of your car bike. And, don’t buy this bike if you like to pedal. It’s too significant and fast. This is a 35 mph roads bike. Also 3 sets of keys?

I did not expect to love this bike as much as I have. It is the perfect train station bike for me, and as a bonus, it is a great way to take my girlfriend to the coffee shop on the weekends. It has fat tires, great suspension, a cushy seat, and strong, smooth acceleration and confidence-inspiring braking. It looks cool enough for the cops to think I’m a kid picking up his girlfriend, and it has so much range that I probably won’t need to charge it monthly. At $1399-$1699 (10% off) depending on battery config, this is less than half the price of some of the pricier and admittedly more stylish Super73 options out there.

I understand that some will fault Engwe for selling a 3.3kW motor e-bike as a class 2 e-bike. But I genuinely feel safer on the road, being able to go at the 35mph speed that cars are going rather than forcing them to go around me. Plus, it isn’t like every single car on the road goes over the speed limit. So why not bikes too?

The Engwe M20 3.0 is over the limit but in all of the best possible ways.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Next Technology Holding (Nasdaq: NXTT) sold about 500 bitcoin last week and noted it will put the money toward artificial intelligence projects, the latest public company to trim its bitcoin treasury as prices slide.
  • In a recent development, the Japan-based software firm disclosed in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday that it sold the coins on Nov.
  • The sale leaves NXTT with 5,333 BTC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Next Technology Holding (Nasdaq: NXTT) sold about 500 bitcoin last week and noted it will put the money toward artificial intelligence projects, the latest public company to trim its bitcoin treasury as prices slide.

In a recent development, the Japan-based software firm disclosed in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday that it sold the coins on Nov. 21 for about $29.22 million. That works out to an average price of $58,468.11 per bitcoin, net of fees and expenses.

The sale leaves NXTT with 5,333 BTC. The manufacturer was paid in tether (USDT), the dollar-pegged stablecoin, rather than in dollars.

NXTT remarked it plans to use the proceeds for research and development of its AI-related initiatives, including its AI software products and services, as well as for general corporate purposes.

In a recent development, the sale is the first under a program the manufacturer’s board approved on Oct. 30. That program allows NXTT to sell or pledge its bitcoin “from time to time in one or more tranches,” through exchange sales, block trades or loans that use the coins as collateral, with the stated aim of “reducing risk exposure and enhancing liquidity.”.

In a recent development, the filing also repeats a line from the company’s latest quarterly report that marks a clear break from its earlier approach. NXTT “does not presently expect to purchase additional Bitcoin,” the company said, adding that it has adjusted its strategy to focus on managing the coins it already holds.

The program has no expiration date and doesn’t require the company to sell any set amount. The board can change, pause or end it at any time. As of Nov. 24, NXTT noted it had not pledged any of its bitcoin as collateral.

Recent findings suggest that NXTT, which is incorporated in Wyoming but based in Saitama Prefecture, Japan, describes itself as running two strategies: AI-enabled software development and holding bitcoin. It keeps substantially all of its coins with Japan-based institutional custodians, according to its quarterly filing.

Recent findings suggest that the organization held 833 BTC at the end of 2024 and added 5,000 BTC in 2025, bringing its total to 5,833 BTC. Its filing puts the cost basis of those coins at about $183.1 million, or roughly $31,400 per bitcoin, meaning last week’s sale still came in well above what the company paid on average.

Sources indicate that falling prices have still hit the books. NXTT reported a net loss of $32.2 million for the first nine months of 2026, compared with net income of $295.1 million a year earlier. The company said the swing came mainly from a drop in the fair value of its digital assets.

The company has also been reshaping its leadership around AI. Earlier this month it named Chan Phang Chuen, a former platform architect focused on computing infrastructure and AI inference, as chief technical officer after Hongliang Liu resigned from the role.

In a recent development, NXTT joins a growing list of public companies selling bitcoin to fund other businesses. Ionic Digital sold 737 bitcoin this month to pay for a data center buildout, and Rumble sold two-thirds of its bitcoin as its AI cloud business delivered its first profitable quarter.

Sources indicate that miners have been selling too. Bitdeer sold all 281 bitcoin it mined last week and now holds none. Not every treasury firm is stepping back, though. Strategy added 457 bitcoin for $29.6 million during the same week NXTT was selling.

Bitcoin has struggled to hold $60,000 this week amid heavy outflows from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs, and NXTT sold its coins near those levels.

The company stated the proceeds from any future sales or pledges will depend on market conditions and the timing of execution.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Core Lightning’s first 26.12 release candidate adds a way to reclaim funds from some pending Bitcoin Lightning payments.
  • It applies after an operator loses local channel data and a peer closes the channel by posting a transaction to Bitcoin.
  • In a recent development, core Lightning published the test build on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Core Lightning’s first 26.12 release candidate adds a way to reclaim funds from some pending Bitcoin Lightning payments.

It applies after an operator loses local channel data and a peer closes the channel by posting a transaction to Bitcoin. The tool gives the operator separate ways to reclaim outgoing funds or collect incoming funds, depending on the payment information that survived.

In a recent development, core Lightning published the test build on Nov. 18, and still headed the project’s release list on Nov. 25 as a pre-release.

Industry observers note that bitcoin Optech covered the feature in its Nov. 20 newsletter and revisited it in its Nov. 24 podcast recap.

Core Lightning’s existing recovery process can reclaim the operator’s main channel balance when the peer posts a closing transaction the recovering node has never seen.

The change adds a fresh tool that addresses a separate output: the amount the closing transaction sets aside for a payment that was still pending.

Industry observers note that both recovery paths require a matching output in the closing transaction that remains unspent. For a payment the operator offered, the tool’s manual says the operator needs the payment hash and the expiry. Once the timelock expires, the operator can reclaim those funds.

For a payment the peer offered, the operator needs the preimage, the secret that matches the payment hash. The operator’s claim must be confirmed on Bitcoin before the peer reclaims the same output. Once the timelock expires, the peer can take the funds back.

The tool reconstructs the spending conditions for each payment the operator wants to recover and checks them against the closing transaction, and skips payments that are too small to have an output.

It produces signed transactions for the operator to review and broadcast manually.

Core Lightning 26.12rc1 tests recovery after an operator loses channel data and the peer force-closes the channel.

The tool handles pending-payment outputs. The main channel balance has its own recovery path.

The original node secret, channel and payment details, and the peer’s public commitment point are also required. Outputs that are absent or already spent cannot be recovered.

The two paths follow the tagged Core Lightning manual’s rules for payments offered by the operator or the closing peer.

Industry observers note that the original node secret, channel and payment details, and the peer’s public commitment point are also required. Outputs that are absent or already spent cannot be recovered.

The operator needs the original node secret, the peer’s closing transaction, channel identifiers and key information, and details for each payment they want to recover.

A cooperating peer can supply the public commitment point tied to the closing transaction while keeping its private keys and commitment secrets private.

Core Lightning’s wallet recovery guide describes using the node secret and an emergency channel backup to reclaim the main balance after a peer closes the channel.

It also warns that restoring an outdated database can permanently lose funds, so recovering a pending payment depends on having enough information to reconstruct its particular output.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a hacker stole customer data, Binance founder Changpeng Zhao advised 1Password consumers to change all the passwords stored in the service.

1Password offered different advice about what users should do after the incident was disclosed on Nov. 25. The password management service said hackers hadn't gained access to the passwords stored in users' vaults, so there was no need to reset them.

According to recent reports, "If you use 1Password, recommend you to change ALL your passwords. It's a pain in the neck, but necessary," Zhao mentioned on X, replying to a post from Coin Bureau about the breach.

If you have a crypto exchange login stored in 1Password, this distinction is vital.

Scammers could still use the stolen email addresses to contact people they know are 1Password users.

In a recent development, 1Password started investigating on Nov. 19 after detecting signs of possible unauthorized access to an employee's corporate GitHub account.

From there, the hacker was able to steal private source code and inject malicious code into 1Password's backend services. The malicious code then downloaded certain administrative data about customers.

Industry observers note that 1Password publicly disclosed the breach on Nov. 25, six days later.

The tech giant did not specify how many customers were affected or explain exactly how the hacker managed to take over the employee's account.

The stolen data included customer names, login email addresses, account and user IDs, and timestamps indicating account creation and last use.

The hacker also gained access to 1Password's software development and deployment systems.

1Password disabled the compromised employee's GitHub account and revoked the stolen access token.

The firm also restored a clean version of the affected service and revoked or replaced potentially exposed internal credentials.

1Password also engaged independent security experts to review its response.

1Password recommends that customers check the 1Password app or type the firm's website address directly into their browser if they receive an unexpected invitation or recovery message.

The tech giant says it will never contact users to request their account password or Secret Key.

Upgrade: 1Password claims that there is no need to change one's 1Password account password or any of the passwords saved in one's vault. No customer passwords were exposed in this incident.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Zonveer ZX3 is one of the best values I’ve seen in electric off-road riding, and one of the most fun things I’ve ridden to date – value for the dollar. Its Black Friday sale brings the 2,800W electric dirt bike down to $1,299, $500 off its $1,799 list price.

For that money, you get a 1,200Wh battery, dual hydraulic disc brakes, and full suspension in a 130 lb package. That’s a great entry point for beginners.

Sources indicate that zonveer is a young brand. It introduced in the US in March with two bikes, the kid-sized DX1 and the ZX3, and it’s run by United Mobility, which lists its address in Dover, Delaware. It sells direct and ships from US warehouses, and Zonveer also sells the ZX3 across Europe under its own brand through its EU store.

Here’s what the ZX3 brings, according to Zonveer’s product page:.

Sources indicate that A hub motor means there’s no motor chain to maintain, and the NFC card and PIN unlock mean there’s no app to fight with. I like that.

Zonveer sent me a ZX3 to test, and I’m impressed with what they shipped, knowing the cost. It isn’t trying to be a race bike. And it doesn’t need to be. Here’s my first ride review:.

It has been revealed that with 2,800W peak, it’s somewhat modest by e-moto standards. That’s exactly what makes it approachable for someone who has never ridden a dirt bike: the power is enough to have a blast on trails without being intimidating.

My girlfriend had never ridden a dirt bike before, and she got comfortable within a few minutes, and she was hooked as soon as she got the hang of it.

It has been revealed that and while testing with my girlfriend, it was clear this bike makes the most sense for lighter riders. Zonveer claims it climbs slopes of up to 30 degrees, which is optimistic for anyone over ~175 lbs, like myself. It still climbed some of the worst slopes on my land, but it did so with some difficulty, which wasn’t the case for some of my lighter friends who also rode it.

Range is the other claim to take with a grain of salt. Riding 45 miles on 1,200Wh means using under 27Wh per mile, which is e-bike efficiency on a 130 lb dirt bike with knobby tires. It’s still a lot of energy, and you can ride this long distances at lower speeds. Just expect less if you ride it hard, and that’s where the fun is at.

Zonveer’s Black Friday sale has the ZX3 at $1,299, and the company gave Electrek readers the code ELECTREK for an extra 5% off, which brings it down to $1,234.05.

The sale also includes a free water bottle and lock, and can be combined for a two-pack of ZX3s for $2,599. Shipping is free, the warranty is one year, Zonveer told us it accepts returns within 30 days on bikes ridden less than 10 miles, with a $200 restocking fee. Here’s the full refund policy.

We’ve ridden a lot of electric two-wheelers, and the ZX3 is one of the most fun per dollar. At $1,299, or about $1,234 with our code, it’s hard to find another 1,200Wh electric dirt bike with dual hydraulic disc brakes and full suspension from a brand that ships from US warehouses.

It has been revealed that it’s not fast by e-moto standards, and the range and climbing claims are optimistic. But for beginners, and especially lighter riders, the power lands right in that sweet spot of manageable fun. It’s a bike you can learn on without scaring yourself, and it’s cheap enough that a family can buy two for less than one Sur-Ron.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • CleanSpark (Nasdaq: CLSK) may sell more bitcoin than it mines as it works to lower risk on its balance sheet, President and CFO Gary Vecchiarelli said Tuesday, after the miner posted a $987.1 million net loss for its fiscal year ended Sept.
  • “We see the selling of a small amount of bitcoin in excess of the quarterly production to be one way of derisking,” Vecchiarelli mentioned on the organization’s earnings call.
  • Vecchiarelli remarked CleanSpark already aims to sell virtually all of the bitcoin it mines to run the business, and that it has sold some bitcoin since year-end to build cash for acquisitions it expects to make soon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CleanSpark (Nasdaq: CLSK) may sell more bitcoin than it mines as it works to lower risk on its balance sheet, President and CFO Gary Vecchiarelli said Tuesday, after the miner posted a $987.1 million net loss for its fiscal year ended Sept. 30, as lower bitcoin prices hit the value of its holdings.

“We see the selling of a small amount of bitcoin in excess of the quarterly production to be one way of derisking,” Vecchiarelli mentioned on the organization’s earnings call. He added that CleanSpark will be “very reactionary to markets” and use that cash to avoid dilution or upcoming debt.

Vecchiarelli remarked CleanSpark already aims to sell virtually all of the bitcoin it mines to run the business, and that it has sold some bitcoin since year-end to build cash for acquisitions it expects to make soon. “It is reasonable to expect that we will fund highly accretive acquisitions and development of projects by selling or borrowing against our bitcoin,” he said.

The Las Vegas-based firm reported full-year revenue of $576.5 million, down 25%. The loss came to $3.74 per basic share, and adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $304.2 million. Vecchiarelli noted about two-thirds of the swing from last year’s $364 million profit came from noncash mark-to-market losses on bitcoin.

According to recent reports, cleanSpark recorded a $281.6 million loss on the fair value of its bitcoin for the year, versus a $425.6 million gain a year earlier. It also took $177.1 million in impairment charges, mostly tied to turning its Sandersville, Georgia, mining site into a data center. Bitcoin ended the fiscal year near $83,600, down from about $114,000, the CFO noted.

The fourth quarter looked different. CleanSpark earned $9.8 million, or 4 cents a share, helped by a $305.6 million gain on its bitcoin, even as revenue dropped 46% from a year earlier to $120.9 million. Analysts had expected a loss of 33 cents a share and revenue of about $134.3 million, Investing.com reported.

In a recent development, the miner produced 7,253 BTC during the year, down 8% as network difficulty rose and it curtailed some machines, and ended September with about 200,000 machines running, down from 225,000 at the end of June. That cut lifted fleet efficiency to 14.8 joules per terahash, while average hashrate fell to 36.0 EH/s.

CleanSpark held 13,530 BTC, including pledged collateral, at the end of September, worth about $1.1 billion then. Its annual report demonstrates it sold 1,532 bitcoin during the year and used another 6,068 to settle derivatives. At Wednesday’s price near $57,700, 13,530 BTC would be worth roughly $780 million.

In a recent development, cleanSpark stock fell to a new 52-week low of $4.43 shortly after Wednesday’s open, before trimming losses to about $4.85 around 10 a.m. ET, down roughly 5% from Tuesday’s $5.12 close, as the Nasdaq sank about 4% at the open. Shares had slipped about 3% in premarket trading.

Sources indicate that at least three firms cut their price targets while keeping buy-equivalent ratings. Needham lowered its target to $15 from $23, citing weaker mining results, while H.C. Wainwright cut to $18 from $22 and Cantor Fitzgerald trimmed to $14 from $19, saying the stock near $5 prices in little beyond Sandersville.

In a recent development, miners broadly are under pressure with bitcoin below $60,000 and down about 24% in November. Bitdeer sold all 281 bitcoin it mined last week, while American Bitcoin lined up a $150 million credit line backed by its BTC. JPMorgan warned in June that mining costs had worsened.

CleanSpark now calls itself an “energy native data center developer.” Its 20-year, $6.6 billion lease at Sandersville is funded by $2.276 billion of 7.875% notes due 2031, and CEO Matt Schultz stated the first data hall is on track for the fourth quarter of 2027.

According to recent reports, texas is moving slower. Exclusivity periods at the Sealy and Brazoria sites, which offer up to 885 MW, expired without a lease. “The Texas regulatory landscape for data center development is evolving, and that has extended project time lines across the state,” Schultz noted on the call.

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that lido voters backed a proposal on Nov.
  • In the March slashing case that prompted the vote, Lido’s contracts automatically recovered about 43% of the loss, while the operator voluntarily covered the rest.
  • According to recent reports, the Snapshot result posted on Lido’s governance forum revealed 53.8 million LDO in favor and 4.1 million against, enough to reach quorum.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that lido voters backed a proposal on Nov. 23 to let the committee overseeing its two community staking modules recover more Ethereum staking losses from operators’ bonds.

In the March slashing case that prompted the vote, Lido’s contracts automatically recovered about 43% of the loss, while the operator voluntarily covered the rest.

According to recent reports, the Snapshot result posted on Lido’s governance forum revealed 53.8 million LDO in favor and 4.1 million against, enough to reach quorum. The off-chain vote backed a wider remit for the committee overseeing Lido’s two open-entry Community Staking Modules, 0x01 and 0x02.

The vote carried zero on-chain actions, so individual penalties must still be reported and settled separately.

The updated mandate extends an existing penalty mechanism used when operators divert block rewards. It would also cover staking rewards missed after slashing, along with incidents that could harm the protocol, such as withdrawal delays or risks to validator key security.

Committee members who backed the change called for documented evidence, credit for losses already recovered, and a chance for operators to respond.

Lido’s final incident report put the March 12 slashing at 0.7973122 ETH in penalties and missed rewards. When the six validators withdrew, Lido’s contracts automatically took 0.3459189 ETH from the operator’s bond to cover the withdrawal shortfall.

The operator voluntarily paid the remaining 0.4513933 ETH after the committee made contact, and Lido reported that the incident was fully resolved in April.

Lido published its final loss figures on April 22.

The amount Lido could collect at settlement would depend on the bond still available.

Sources indicate that this graphic describes one resolved incident. Percentages are rounded.

In a recent development, use Lido’s April 22 final accounting for the March 12 incident. Divide each reported amount by 0.7973122 ETH and round to the nearest whole percent for labels. Bar segment widths use the unrounded shares.

Recent findings suggest that this graphic describes one resolved incident. Percentages are rounded.

In a recent development, in a similar case under the wider mandate, the committee could assess the missed rewards separately and lock collateral against that amount. The amount Lido could collect at settlement would depend on the bond left after the automatic deduction.

It has been revealed that under the penalty procedure, the report locks the assessed loss and any applicable fine, and the operator can compensate Lido or dispute the report. The committee can start an Easy Track motion to settle the penalty.

Industry observers note that the locked collateral is burned when the motion is enacted, and Lido’s Easy Track rules give LDO holders at least 72 hours to object. Objections backed by at least 0.5% of total LDO supply stop the motion.

Industry observers note that the bond backs all validators run under the same operator account in a module. Lido sizes the required collateral by the number of keys the operator runs.

In 0x01, a default operator posts 2.4 ETH for the first 32 ETH validator and 1.3 ETH for each additional key. The 0x02 module requires 32 ETH for the first key and 30 ETH for each additional key.

A 0x02 validator receives 32 ETH to start and can receive more stake after activation without increasing the required bond.

At the theoretical 2,048 ETH effective-balance ceiling, the 32 ETH first-key bond would equal about 1.56% of that balance. The 2.4 ETH first-key bond in 0x01 equals 7.5% of the validator’s 32 ETH balance.

Lido released 0x02 on Oct. 23, and its October operator update reported nearly 800,000 ETH being validated in the established module. The first 30 keys in 0x02 had received seed deposits, or 960 ETH in all, with 54 more keys still queued at the time.

In a recent development, kvorum’s record of a separate Nov. 18 motion shows the 0x02 allocation limit rose from 0.01% to 0.5% of Lido’s core pool. The higher limit lets the module take on more stake as deposits arrive.

Lido’s operator documentation says the collateral is held in stETH. If an assessed penalty exceeds the available bond, the excess becomes debt that can be recovered from future rewards or bond top-ups.

Queued keys that lose bond coverage stop receiving deposits, and unbonded validators can face exit requests. How much and how quickly the protocol can recover depends on what the operator has left in the bond and what comes in later.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, U.S. spot exchange-traded funds for XRP recorded net inflows of $4.07 million on Nov. 25. XRP was the only cryptocurrency among the 10 ETF categories tracked in a SoSoValue snapshot shared by BankXRP to register net inflows.

Wednesday's inflows narrowed the net outflow gap for XRP ETFs. Following the latest inflows, XRP funds had recorded $21.25 million more in investor outflows than inflows over the 30 days ending Nov. 25.

Sources indicate that that means the net outflows over the rest of the period totaled $25.32 million. In a single trading day, investors covered about 16% of that shortfall.

The five U.S. spot XRP ETFs tracked by SoSoValue presently have total net assets of $1.04 billion. This is marginally higher than the $1 billion held by nine spot Solana ETFs.

Industry observers note that however, there is a larger disparity in cumulative net inflows between XRP and Solana funds. Cumulative net inflows total $1.79 billion for XRP and $1.51 billion for Solana.

The two figures measure different things. Cumulative net inflows represent the total amount of money invested in the funds minus redemptions.

Sources indicate that net assets, on the other hand, represent the current value of a fund's holdings. This figure changes with the price of XRP.

This explains why XRP funds have a little over $1 billion in net assets despite attracting nearly $1.8 billion in cumulative net inflows.

Trading activity was slightly higher in Solana ETFs on Wednesday, with total volume reaching $35.54 million, compared to $33.40 million for XRP.

However, Solana ETFs recorded zero net flows for the day.

Investors can trade existing ETF shares with one another without affecting the total amount of money invested in the funds.

The contrast with Bitcoin ETFs was stark.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $123.41 million in net outflows on Wednesday, according to preliminary figures reported by SoSoValue.

Recent findings suggest that however, the total for Bitcoin was still being compiled when BankXRP shared the numbers. SoSoValue marked the XRP total as complete.

Recent findings suggest that with U.S. markets closed for Thanksgiving, XRP ETF buyers have only one more trading day this week.

Trading resumes on U.S. equity markets on Friday, Nov. 27. However, the session will end early, with markets closing at 1 p.m. Eastern time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that tesla has pulled the $41,990 Model Y All-Wheel Drive from its US online configurator.
  • The trim lasted just over nine months.
  • Here’s what Tesla’s US Model Y design studio lists as of today (prices before the destination fee):.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that tesla has pulled the $41,990 Model Y All-Wheel Drive from its US online configurator. The cheapest dual-motor Model Y you can order now is the Model Y Premium AWD at $49,990, an $8,000 jump.

The trim lasted just over nine months. Tesla launched it in early February, and it’s gone without a word from the company.

Here’s what Tesla’s US Model Y design studio lists as of today (prices before the destination fee):.

It has been revealed that when Tesla debuted the base Model Y AWD in February, it was basically the stripped-down Model Y with a second motor. It had 294 miles of range, did 0-60 mph in 4.6 seconds and kept the same cut-down cabin as the base RWD. At a $2,000 premium over the single-motor version, it was the most sensible AWD pricing Tesla had offered in years.

According to recent reports, and the AWD trim isn’t the only change. In February, the Premium RWD cost $44,990 and the Premium AWD cost $48,990. Both are now $1,000 higher.

Add it up and the cheapest all-wheel-drive Model Y went from $41,990 to $49,990 in nine months. That’s a 19% increase.

The timing isn’t great for Tesla’s competitive position. Chevrolet’s 2027 Equinox EV LT 1 AWD starts at $40,295 before destination, with 307 miles of EPA range. Ford’s Mustang Mach-E Select AWD starts at $40,795.

Both now undercut Tesla’s cheapest AWD crossover by more than $9,000.

If you live somewhere it snows and you were shopping for a new Model Y, the math just got a lot worse. You can still find some base AWD units in Tesla’s inventory, but once those are gone, that’s it.

In a recent development, this is also the latest cut in a year of Tesla shrinking its lineup. Elon Musk killed the Model S and Model X in January to free up Fremont for Optimus, and Cybertruck production is winding down. Meanwhile, the most recent latest Tesla is the $61,990 Model Y L, which sits at the top of the range, not the bottom.

Sources indicate that we liked this trim. It was the first time in a long time that Tesla treated all-wheel drive as a $2,000 option rather than a huge upsell bundled with a nicer interior, and it put the Model Y right in the price bracket of the Equinox EV and Mach-E with AWD.

Now it’s gone, and the Premium trims went up $1,000 on top of that. Tesla didn’t explain either move. It rarely does anymore.

In a recent development, there are two plausible reasons. Either Tesla is tight on Model Y build slots and would rather fill them with higher-margin Premium trims, or the cheap AWD simply wasn’t selling. We don’t know which. But both explanations land in the same place for buyers: a more expensive Model Y.

Sources indicate that tesla is not going to keep 6 different model Y trims especially when the most expensive trim in the Model YL is selling. They will definitely squeeze out as much money from selling more expensive trims so the lowest end trim will most likely be next to go.

It has been revealed that and Tesla has a habit of this. The “Standard” name for its cheaper Model Y and Model 3 lasted a few months. The single-motor Cybertruck, the only version that made sense, was gone within days. Cheaper trims show up, get a news cycle, and quietly disappear.

It has been revealed that that’s a problem for a company whose consumer lineup is shrinking down to two cars. The Model Y is Tesla’s volume. Thinning it out at the bottom is the opposite of what you’d do if growing EV sales were the priority.

How long before the $39,990 RWD goes the same way?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Electric truck operator Nevoya is expanding its deal with Meta with the fresh deployment of 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on the Interstate 10 (I-10) between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona … but Meta won’t be shipping any products.

The second major trucking deal between Facebook parent firm Meta and electric truck operator Nevoya will put 25 latest battery-electric semis on I-10, running freight between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona. But Meta isn’t buying trucks, hiring drivers or shipping its own products. Instead, Zuck’s company helping pay for someone else’s cleaner freight through environmental attribute certificates (EACs), a carbon credit mechanism that lets companies claim the emissions benefits of electric trucking without operating the trucks themselves.

Recent findings suggest that “Coming back to Nevoya for a second corridor reflects what we look for in our value chain work: partners that can scale, and agreements we can repeat, stated Devon Lake, Head of Net Zero Strategy, Meta. “Freight is part of the emissions footprint of building and operating our data centers, and multi-year commitments like this help address our scope 3 emissions and make electric trucking available and competitive on the routes that serve the regions where we build.”.

Meta was one of several buyers in the DC-based Center for Green Market Activation (GMA) buyers’ alliance. The group’s collective EAC purchases supported Nevoya’s initial 63-truck deployment on the Houston–Dallas corridor back in May. This latest Agreement, however, is a standalone deal between Nevoya and Meta only, and gives Meta an established framework to open more electric truck corridors in the future.

This clever application of these agreements is what makes the Dallas-Houston run stand out, with GMA calling it, “the first large-scale application of book and claim to zero-emission trucking.” The firm adds that this arrangement helps client companies overcome existing barriers to EV adoption while enabling Nevoya to deploy upcoming trucks, “where they deliver the strongest commercial and operational value.”.

Industry News: HRF Confirms Funding of Seven Bitcoin Projects for People Living Under Authoritarian Regimes
